papers.title: From Genes to Neural Circuits: Genetic and Systems Mechanisms of Ethanol Sensitivity and Tolerance in Drosophila melanogaster.
papers.abstract: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is a complex neuropsychiatric disease shaped by genetic, environmental, and physiological factors. Over four decades, Drosophila melanogaster has emerged as a powerful model for dissecting the molecular and neural mechanisms underlying ethanol sensitivity, tolerance, preference, and consumption. Its conserved signaling pathways, sophisticated genetic toolkit, and robust behavioral assays have enabled discovery of genes and neural circuits governing alcohol responses across biological levels. This review summarizes major advances in the genetics and neurobiology of ethanol-related behaviors in Drosophila. Forward genetic screens identified conserved regulators of ethanol sensitivity and tolerance, including cAMP/PKA signaling components, ion channels, neurotransmitter receptors, cytoskeletal regulators, and neuropeptide pathways. Subsequent studies revealed distinct roles for the ellipsoid body, mushroom bodies, circadian neurons, and barrier glia in intoxication, tolerance, and reward. Epigenetic studies further established chromatin remodeling and transcriptional regulation as mechanisms of long-term behavioral plasticity, while systems genetics and genome-wide association studies highlighted the polygenic basis of natural variation in alcohol-related traits. Together, these findings advance an integrated view of ethanol action and provide a framework for understanding human AUD. Emerging approaches include single-cell and connectomics analyses, functional testing of human variants, and integration of systems genetics with circuit neuroscience.

papers.title: Progress in research on the bidirectional relationship between circadian rhythm and depression: A bibliometric analysis.
papers.abstract: This study used VOSviewer and CiteSpace to conduct a bibliometric analysis of 444 publications on the relationship between circadian rhythms and depression, retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection (January 2015 to April 2025). Publication numbers remained low until 2017 but increased markedly after 2018, with the United States contributing the largest share. Ian B. Hickie and Joanne S. Carpenter were the most prolific authors; the University of Pittsburgh and Chronobiology International were the most productive institution and journal, respectively. McClung, Dubocovich, and Logan were the top co-cited authors, while frequent keywords included "expression," "sleep," "circadian rhythms," and "melatonin." These findings underscore the growing importance of circadian rhythms in depression pathophysiology and therapy, with future research likely to focus on diagnosis, biomarker identification, individualized treatment, prognosis, and health management.

papers.title: Additive Effects of Time Awake and Number of Flights on Fatigue in Short-Haul Pilots: Implications for Duty Time Regulation.
papers.abstract: Time awake affects airline pilots' fatigue but it is less clear how workload during that time awake impacts fatigue. Although current flight time limitations take the number of flights within a duty period as a measure of workload into account, quantitative evidence for its fatiguing effect is scarce. Here, we analysed fatigue, subjective workload and flight-associated hassles at the end of 553 short-haul flights from 37 airline pilots. Two linear mixed-models with fatigue or subjective workload as the dependent variable were generated, adjusted for time awake, number of completed flights, number of hassles, prior sleep and pilot's responsibility (flying/monitoring). Results showed that fatigue was influenced by time awake, number of flights and pilot's responsibility, whereas no effect was found for number of hassles. The critical fatigue threshold (flying not recommended) was exceeded 2.4 h earlier when operating four flights compared with one flight. Fatigue was lower but subjective workload was higher when the pilot was flying instead of monitoring. Subjective workload increased with number of hassles, but not with number of flights or time awake. European duty time limitations are justified to include a penalty for additional flights but may underestimate the fatiguing effect.

papers.title: Sleep, inflammation, and pain in musculoskeletal rehabilitation: a structured integrative review of neurobiological mechanisms and non-pharmacological pain management strategies.
papers.abstract: Sleep disturbance, inflammation, and persistent pain may reinforce one another, compromising musculoskeletal rehabilitation. To synthesize evidence on mechanisms linking sleep, inflammation, and pain and identify relevant non-pharmacological interventions. This structured integrative review examined peer-reviewed studies published from January 2010 to December 2025, identified through PubMed, Scopus, PEDro, and SciELO. Reporting and synthesis were guided by SANRA and EQUATOR recommendations. Fifty-seven studies were included: 24 experimental or observational studies, 17 systematic reviews or meta-analyses, and 16 narrative or integrative reviews. Sleep restriction was associated with changes in interleukin-6, tumor necrosis factor-α, and C-reactive protein, with responses varying across populations and protocols. Prostaglandins and bradykinin may promote nociceptive sensitization, while disrupted sleep may impair descending pain inhibition. Exercise, manual therapy, neuromuscular electrical stimulation, low-level laser therapy, and sleep-focused behavioral interventions showed mechanistic plausibility, although confirmatory trials remain limited. Sleep assessment and sleep-focused interventions should be considered within multimodal musculoskeletal pain management, while further controlled research clarifies clinical effectiveness.

papers.title: Beyond seasonality: Rethinking daylight exposure in adolescent sleep research.
The association of particulate matter 2.5 exposure with frailty trajectories in middle-aged and older Chinese adults and the potential modification by lifestyle and socioeconomic status.
papers.abstract: To examine PM2.5 exposure associations with frailty trajectories in middle-aged and older Chinese adults, and evaluate modifying effects of lifestyle and socioeconomic status (SES). We analyzed 10,659 participants from CHARLS using PM2.5 data from Dalhousie University. Frailty was assessed via a deficit accumulation index. Group-based trajectory modelling (GBTM) identified frailty trajectories; ordered logistic regression estimated associations and effect modifications. Three trajectories emerged: "Stable low" (63.95%), "Increased to frailty" (29.00%), and "Continuously worsening" (7.05%). Each 10 μg/m³ PM2.5 increase raised odds of Trajectories 2 and 3 by 15.2% and 12.3%, respectively. Higher SES attenuated PM2.5 effects (RERI=-0.067), while unhealthy sleep duration amplified them (RERI=0.163). PM2.5 exposure is associated with deteriorating frailty trajectories. Higher SES exerts an antagonistic effect, whereas unhealthy sleep duration has a synergistic effect on PM2.5-related frailty progression.

papers.title: Relationship between objective sleep efficiency and psychological distress in middle-aged and older Japanese: Results by work in the Shika study.
papers.abstract: Sleep quality and work, as factors related to psychological distress, have not yet been elucidated. Additionally, few studies have examined the association between sleep efficiency and psychological distress, which may affect psychological distress in middle-aged and older adults according to their work status. This study aimed to examine and clarify the relationship between sleep efficiency and psychological distress in middle-aged and older Japanese stratified by work and sex. A cross-sectional study was performed among community dwellers aged 40-90 years living in Shika-machi, Ishikawa, Japan, between January 2018 and April 2020. Psychological distress was assessed utilizing the Kessler 6 scale (K6), a psychological distress scale. Sleep efficiency was measured using actigraphy (MTI-220, ACOS Co., Ltd., Nagano, Japan) that includes the sleep index, and analyses were stratified by work status and sex. A multiple logistic regression analysis was conducted setting the high K6 group as an objective variable. A total of 360 middle-aged and older adults (women = 54.4%; mean age = 63.09 ± 10.48 years) were included in this study. Psychological distress, adjusted for confounders, was associated with low sleep efficiency (β = -0.060, p = 0.013) only among working women. We found no evidence of a relationship between other indicators of psychological distress in men with or without work and women without work. These results reveal a relationship between psychological distress and sleep efficiency among middle-aged and older working women, suggesting that work and poor sleep efficiency may be associated with greater psychological distress. Future studies should examine the relationship between psychological distress and sleep efficiency in women middle-aged and older using longitudinal studies that consider work-related effects.

papers.title: Unilateral nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy associated with obstructive sleep apnea-hypopnea syndrome: a case report.
papers.abstract: This report describes a case of obstructive sleep apnea-hypopnea syndrome (OSAHS) associated with nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION). NAION is an optic neuropathy characterized by painless vision loss, visual field defects, and optic disc edema. It results from hypoperfusion of the short posterior ciliary arteries, leading to acute ischemia and structural and functional impairment of the optic nerve, which ultimately manifests as blurred vision or blindness. We report the case of a 59-year-old Han Chinese male who presented with a 6-day history of blurred vision and visual field defects in the left eye. The diagnosis was confirmed after excluding other potential etiologies. The patient was treated with 80 mg of oral methylprednisolone, which was gradually tapered, alongside neuroprotective and circulation-improving therapies. Following consultation with the Department of Respiratory and Sleep Medicine, he was initiated on noninvasive ventilation (NIV) to correct systemic hypoxia and received bronchodilators. Subsequently, the patient's symptoms showed moderate improvement. NAION is frequently associated with a variety of systemic vascular risk factors, particularly hypertension, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, ischemic heart disease, and cerebrovascular disease. These conditions compromise the microvascular supply to the optic nerve head, leading to ischemia, necrosis, and subsequent optic atrophy. Among these, OSAHS is recognized as a significant and independent risk factor. OSAHS is a clinical syndrome characterized by recurrent episodes of apnea and hypopnea during sleep, resulting in intermittent hypoxia, hypercapnia, and sleep fragmentation. OSAHS is a well-established risk factor for systemic vascular comorbidities, including cardiovascular disease and diabetes mellitus. In the present case, an association between OSAHS and NAION was observed after excluding other potential confounding etiologies. These findings highlight the clinical importance of screening for and managing OSAHS in patients with NAION, providing a rationale for optimized therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Association of insomnia with anxiety might be greater than that of depression among patients with gastrointestinal cancer: a network analysis.
papers.abstract: Patients with gastrointestinal cancer frequently encounter a myriad of sleep disorders, and these disturbances can profoundly exacerbate their psychological distress, particularly anxiety and depression. Elucidating the intricate relationship between sleep disorders and psychological disturbances holds paramount significance in enhancing the therapeutic efficacy and improving the survival outcomes for these patients. A cross-sectional study including 352 participants from two hospitals was conducted. Insomnia symptoms and psychological distress were assessed. Pearson correlation analysis and network analysis were used to determine the association between insomnia and psychological distress components. In this study, the prevalence of psychological distress was recorded at 45.2%, while the prevalence of difficulty initiating sleep (DIS), difficulty maintaining sleep (DMS), and early morning awakening (EMA) stood at 37.5%, 34.9%, and 46.9%, respectively. The partial correlation showed the strongest correlation was observed between DIS and anxiety, with a coefficient of 0.15 (0.00, 0.23), and no direct conditional association was observed between depression and any of the insomnia symptoms within the network analyzed. Emphasizing the crucial role of difficulty initiating sleep (DIS) in relation to anxiety deepens our understanding of the intricate interplay between physical and mental symptoms experienced by gastrointestinal cancer patients. By recognizing and comprehending these interconnected factors, healthcare professionals can devise more tailored therapeutic strategies, ultimately contributing to enhanced overall patient outcomes.

papers.title: Motor network neurophysiological (TMS-EEG) markers as predictors of outcomes of ventriculoperitoneal shunt sustained for over a year in normal pressure hydrocephalus.
papers.abstract: Current practice for normal pressure hydrocephalus (NPH) relies on clinical presentation, imaging, and various clinical procedures to determine the need for neurosurgical intervention, specifically the installation of a ventriculoperitoneal shunt (VPS). This study aimed to evaluate the utility of a TMS-evoked potential (TEP)-based assessment (Delphi-MD) for predicting sustained response (over one year) to VPS, serving as an ancillary test to the cerebrospinal fluid tap test (CTT). Forty-one patients with possible iNPH underwent Delphi-MD evaluation of wave form adherence (WFA), a composite measure assessing how closely their TEPs resembled an ideal benchmark TEP. Of these, 18 patients received VPS treatment following a multidisciplinary team decision based on standard practice, blinded to the TEP results. Response to the intervention was evaluated over a period of more than one year using the clinical global impression of change (CGIC) scale, in addition to assessments with a 10-meter timed up and go test and the modified Rankin scale. Responders had higher M1L WFA values at baseline (prior to VPS) than non-responders (median 0.51 [95% CI 0.36-0.76], median 0.14 [95% CI -0.02-0.38], respectively p = 0.012). M1L WFA was successful in distinguishing responders (11/18) from non-responders (7/18) with an ROC-AUC of 0.935 [bootstrap 95% CI 0.792-1.00], p < 0.0001. M1L WFA cutoff was established with LOOCV and produced 90.9% sensitivity, 85.7% specificity and 88.9% accuracy. In contrast the CTT result was unsuccessful in predicting shunt responsiveness. This study indicates that higher M1L WFA obtained through Delphi-MD (TMS-EEG), signifies better preservation and functional integrity of the motor network in patients with probable iNPH that had a sustained response to VPS than those that did not. Given replication of results in future independent cohorts, Delphi-MD shows promise as an objective, accurate, and accessible ancillary screening tool for iNPH candidates, prior to referral for VPS treatment. Registration number: MOH_2021-12-08_010449. Registration date: 11.09.2021. https://clinicaltrial.health.gov.il/clinicaltrials/?sort=experimentapproveddate_tdt+desc&page=1&searchQuery=MOH_2021-12-08_010449 .

papers.title: EEG-defined differences in functional networks following beta-band transcranial alternating current stimulation in patients with disorders of consciousness: a pilot study.
papers.abstract: Severe disruption of cortico-thalamocortical circuits underlies disorders of consciousness (DOC). Beta-band (20 Hz) transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) can be used to probe frontal oscillatory synchrony, yet its potential to acutely modulate large-scale network dynamics in DOC is unknown. We applied 20 Hz tACS (1 mA) for 30 min over the frontal cortex (F3 and F4, International 10-20 system) in 28 patients with DOC. Offline functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) was used to quantify hemoglobin (HbO)-based functional connectivity (FC) and graph-theoretical network properties, including small-world properties (clustering coefficient, Cp; path length, Lp) and global efficiency (global efficiency, Eg; local efficiency, Eloc) at pre-stimulation resting-state measurement for 5 min (pre-stim), the first post-stimulation resting-state measurement for 5 min (post-stim1), and the second post-stimulation resting-state measurement for 5 min (post-stim2). Subgroups were defined by baseline video-electroencephalography (vEEG) pathology as moderately abnormal (n = 11) and diffuse slowing (n = 14); 3 patients excluded (incomplete vEEG). Frontal 20 Hz tACS was associated with transient enhancement of FC across the measured cortical network at post-stim1 (pFDR < 0.05), selectively strengthening intra-and interhemispheric and intra-nodal connectivity before resolving by post-stim2. Crucially, the effects were pathology-dependent, and visual-motor integration pathways (right occipital lobe to left motor cortex; right primary somatosensory cortex to left occipital lobe) emerged exclusively in DOC patients with moderately abnormal background but not in those with diffuse slowing. Concurrent acute network reorganization at post-stim1 (all p < 0.05) featured increased Cp, Eg, and Eloc, along with decreased Lp, all normalizing by post-stim2. Clinically, Coma Recovery Scale-Revised scores correlated positively with average FC of HbO (pre-stim: r = 0.47; post-stim2: r = 0.41) and Area Under the Curve (AUC) of Eg (pre-stim: r = 0.44), and negatively with AUC of Lp (pre-stim: r = - 0.41; all p < 0.05). Frontal beta-tACS was associated with state-dependent changes in functional network organization in DOC, with dynamic fNIRS measures that may be useful for tracking these changes. These findings provide preliminary descriptive evidence of short-term network changes associated with beta-tACS and may help guide future controlled studies of targeted neuromodulation in patients with DOC.

papers.title: EEG microstate alterations in psychotic depression: prolonged microstate C duration and associations with psychotic symptoms.
papers.abstract: Major Depressive Disorder with psychotic features (MDD-Psy) represents a severe clinical subtype with distinct psychopathology, yet its underlying large-scale brain network dynamics, as measured by resting-state EEG microstates, remain poorly characterized. We compared 68 patients with MDD-Psy and 63 patients with MDD without psychotic features (MDD-NonPsy). Clinical assessment included the Kangduo Antidepressant Scale (KDAS) and the Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale (BPRS). Resting-state EEG microstate parameters (duration, time coverage, occurrence, and transition probabilities) were analyzed. Group comparisons employed Mann-Whitney U/t-tests with False Discovery Rate (FDR) correction. Correlations between microstate alterations and psychotic symptom severity were assessed using Spearman's rank correlation with FDR correction. The groups were comparable in age and sex. The MDD-Psy group exhibited significantly greater severity in thought disturbance, activation, and hostility (all p < 0.001). EEG microstate analysis revealed a significantly prolonged median duration of microstate C, putatively associated with salience-network-related activity in MDD-Psy (91.99 ms) versus MDD-NonPsy (85.56 ms; p-corr = 0.004). Altered transition probabilities characterized MDD-Psy, including increased B→A but decreased B→C and C→A transitions (all p-corr < 0.05). Furthermore, in the combined sample, the duration of microstate C positively correlated with thought disturbance (ρ = 0.243, p-FDR = 0.030), while the reduced B→C transition probability was strongly negatively correlated with both thought disturbance (ρ=-0.393, p-FDR < 0.001) and hostility. Within patients with major depressive disorder, the psychotic subtype is associated with a distinct pattern of aberrant resting-state brain network dynamics relative to the non-psychotic subtype, characterized by prolonged microstate C duration, commonly linked to salience network dynamics and reconfigured temporal transitions between the salience, visual, and auditory networks. The altered visual-to-salience network transition (B → C) demonstrated the most robust association with core psychotic symptom dimensions, including thought disturbance and hostility. These findings suggest that dysregulated dynamic coupling between perceptual processing and salience evaluation may represent a candidate neurophysiological indicator of psychotic features in depression. However, these results should be considered hypothesis-generating preliminary: the high rate of antipsychotic medication use in the MDD-Psy group, the absence of a healthy control group, and the cross-sectional design preclude tentative causal or specificity claims. Future longitudinal studies incorporating medication-naïve patients, healthy controls, and complementary neurophysiological markers are required to validate the clinical utility of these microstate alterations. Not applicable.

papers.title: The association between honey consumption amount and physical activity, sleep quality, and Nottingham health profile in young adults.
papers.abstract: Honey is a natural food with potential beneficial effects on health-related behaviors and well-being. However, evidence regarding the association between the amount of honey consumption and physical activity, sleep quality, and health-related quality of life in young adults remains limited. This study aimed to investigate the association between daily honey consumption and physical activity levels, sleep quality, and health-related quality of life among young adults. This cross-sectional comparative study was conducted in January 2026 among university students attending a public university in eastern Türkiye and residing in state dormitories. The required sample size was estimated as 336 through power analysis, and the study was completed with 468 participants. Participants were classified into five groups according to daily honey consumption level: non-consumers, 10, 20, 30, and 40 g per day. Data were collected using the International Physical Activity Questionnaire (IPAQ), the Richards-Campbell Sleep Questionnaire (RCSQ), and the Nottingham Health Profile (NHP). Data were analyzed using one-way ANOVA, correlation, and regression analyses. Most participants had a normal body mass index (BMI), and the mean age was comparable across groups. Among honey consumers, IPAQ scores were positively correlated with RCSQ scores (r = 0.27, p < 0.01), while significant negative correlations were found between IPAQ and NHP, and between RCSQ and NHP (r=-0.26 and r=-0.58, respectively; p < 0.01). Among non-consumers, the correlation between IPAQ and RCSQ was negative and non-significant (r=-0.03, p > 0.05), the correlation between IPAQ and NHP was positive and non-significant (r = 0.02, p > 0.05), and the correlation between RCSQ and NHP was significantly negative (r=-0.29, p < 0.01). Regression analyses indicated that honey consumption level was significantly associated with physical activity, accounting for 6.8% of the variance in IPAQ scores (F = 16.02, p < 0.01), with sleep quality, accounting for 6.4% of the variance in RCSQ scores (F = 31.60, p < 0.01), and with health-related quality of life, accounting for 8.2% of the variance in NHP scores (F = 19.68, p < 0.01). In young adults, daily honey consumption is associated with higher physical activity levels, better sleep quality, and a more favorable symptom burden as assessed by the NHP. Moreover, honey consumption level was significantly associated with variation in these health-related behaviors.

papers.title: Integrating task-state electroencephalography and motor function for intelligent assessment of recovery status from prolonged disorders of consciousness.
papers.abstract: Accurately assessing recovery in patients with prolonged disorders of consciousness (PDoC) is essential for evaluating the therapeutic efficacy and optimizing clinical care. However, substantial individual variability and poorly understood recovery mechanisms render this task exceptionally challenging. We collected task-state electroencephalography and clinical records from 78 PDoC patients to develop an intelligent assessment framework. Power spectral densities (PSDs) and coherence values (CVs) derived from event-related potentials (ERPs) were extracted and integrated with motor function scores to construct a multidimensional feature set. Linear support vector machine (SVM) and logistic regression (LR) models were built and rigorously evaluated via leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV). SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was utilized for visual explanation. The LOOCV indicated that both LR and SVM achieved optimal, similar performance in integrating alpha-band features with motor function (Macro-Average F1-score [Ma-F]: 76.79% versus 75.54%). The Receiver Operating Characteristic curves (with Area Under the Curve values of 77.57% for LR and 72.82% for SVM) and Precision-Recall curves (with Average Precision values of 68.87% for LR and 59.85% for SVM) suggested that the framework performs stably. The reliability curves indicated that both models demonstrate good calibration and are reliable for assessment. The study provides preliminary evidence that alpha-band PSDs and CVs derived from ERPs potentially enhance the motor function assessment performance. This integrated paradigm provides a valuable indicator. Overall, our findings suggest that combining neuroscience with intelligent technology holds promise for improving personalized diagnosis and optimizing the PDoC management.

papers.title: Effect of aerobic and Pilates exercise on balance, gait, functional capacity, lower extremity strength, fear of falling, sleep quality, and quality of life in older adults.
papers.abstract: The primary objective was to compare the effects of aerobic and Pilates exercise programs on balance, gait performance, functional capacity, lower extremity strength, fear of falling, sleep quality, and quality of life in older adults. A secondary objective was to determine which exercise modality yields greater improvements in these outcomes, thereby providing evidence to guide the selection of effective exercise interventions for promoting health and well-being among the older adults. Forty-four older adults, aged 60-69 years, were randomly assigned into either the aerobic (n = 22) or Pilates exercise group (n = 22). The aerobic group trained three sessions per week (30 min of active exercise per session; 90 min/week), while the Pilates group (PG) trained two sessions per week (45 min of active exercise per session comprising mat, standing, and TheraBand components; 90 min/week), each for eight weeks, yielding equivalent total active exercise volumes (720 min per group). The outcomes of Mini-Balance Evaluation System Test (MBEST), Timed Up and Go test (TUGT), 2-Minute Walk Test (2MWT), 10-Meter Walk Test (10MWT), Five-Time Sit-to-Stand test (5xSTST) and self-reported questionnaires of the Fall Efficacy Scale International (FES-I), Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and WHOQOL-Brief were collected at baseline and post-treatment. Groups were equivalent at baseline across all measures. Significant Group × Time interaction effects were observed for gait velocity (10MWT) and dynamic balance (MBEST), with the aerobic group demonstrating significantly greater improvements in both (10MWT: p = 0.016; MBEST: p < 0.001). ANCOVA adjusting for baseline score, age, and BMI confirmed these between-group differences (10MWT: p = 0.012; MBEST: p < 0.001). Significant time main effects (p < 0.05) were observed for all remaining outcome measures (TUGT, 5×STST, 2MWT, FES-I, PSQI, all WHOQOL-Brief domains), indicating meaningful within-group improvements shared across both interventions. Both aerobic and Pilates exercise programs produced clinically meaningful improvements in gait velocity, functional capacity, and balance in older adults, with the aerobic group demonstrating significantly greater improvements in dynamic balance. Both interventions additionally reduced fall-risk classifications based on clinical threshold analyses. The findings of this study suggest that aerobic exercise may be the preferred modality for optimizing functional mobility and balance in community-dwelling older adults, though both modalities offer valuable and clinically meaningful health benefits. Future trials equalizing both volume and frequency are warranted to confirm modality-specific effects with full design equivalence. This Clinical Trial is registered with Thai Clinical Trials Registry (TCTR) approved by WHO. Registration number TCTR20240403002. Date of registration 13 March 2024. URL https//www.thaiclinicaltrials.org/#.

papers.title: Portable polysomnography-derived multi-domain EEG markers of anesthetic state transitions during propofol anesthesia for gastrointestinal endoscopy.
papers.abstract: Propofol anesthesia is widely used for gastrointestinal (GI) endoscopy, but electroencephalographic (EEG) features of anesthetic state transitions in this brief and stimulus-rich setting remain incompletely characterized. This study aimed to describe clinically interpretable EEG markers across anesthetic stages using portable polysomnography (PSG)-derived six-channel EEG. In this prospective observational study, 31 adults undergoing GI endoscopy under propofol-based anesthesia underwent continuous portable PSG recording. EEG analyses focused on six scalp channels (F3, F4, C3, C4, O1, and O2) across four clinically defined stages: baseline, induction, maintenance, and recovery. Relative spectral power, spectral edge frequency at 95% cumulative power (SEF95), and spindle-like event metrics were quantified. Sensor-level functional connectivity was assessed using weighted phase-lag index, imaginary coherence, and amplitude envelope correlation (AEC). Spectral and spindle-like event measures were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models, and connectivity differences were assessed using permutation-based paired tests with false discovery rate correction. Relative delta power decreased from baseline and induction to maintenance and recovery, whereas theta, alpha, sigma, and beta relative power and SEF95 generally increased. Spindle-like event density differed across stages and was highest during recovery, while mean duration and peak frequency remained relatively stable within the 11-16 Hz range. Functional connectivity showed metric-specific modulation: AEC demonstrated the most widespread stage-related differences, whereas phase-based connectivity measures showed only limited edge-specific changes after correction for multiple comparisons. Portable PSG-derived six-channel EEG captured stage-related spectral, spindle-like event, and sensor-level connectivity changes during propofol anesthesia for GI endoscopy. These findings identify candidate EEG features for future evaluation of emergence detection and atypical anesthetic-state identification during procedural anesthesia. Their utility for real-time propofol titration or excessive-sedation warning requires prospective validation.

papers.title: Theta-Band Temporal Interference Stimulation Modulates Food Reward Prediction Error Encoding in Individuals with Elevated Food Addiction Symptoms.
papers.abstract: Prediction error (PE) signals support feedback evaluation and adaptive updating, and are closely linked to medial frontal theta dynamics, particularly within dorsal anterior cingulate cortex (dACC)-centered networks. However, evidence linking these oscillatory mechanisms to the modulation of PE encoding remains limited. Here, we tested whether theta-band modulation of a dACC-centered medial frontal network altered trial-level PE encoding during food-reward processing. In a single-blind, sham-controlled pre-post design, individuals with elevated food addiction symptoms performed a food incentive-delay task while undergoing electroencephalographic recordings combined with theta-band temporal interference stimulation. Single-trial analyses revealed that feedback-related negativity (FRN) amplitudes varied as a function of both behavioral and model-derived prediction errors. Critically, theta-band modulation altered FRN-PE coupling, with the effect most pronounced for unfavorable outcomes, whereas anticipatory activity remained unchanged. These findings support the hypothesis that theta-band modulation can alter feedback-related PE encoding within this population and task context.

papers.title: Dynamics-informed machine learning for recovering extensive missing systems dynamics.
papers.abstract: Inevitable missing values in observational time series often hinder reliable data-driven modeling of complex systems across diverse domains. Recovery is essential yet challenging, particularly in high-dimensional systems where most variables can exhibit extensive intra-series missingness and widespread inter-variable missingness simultaneously. In this study, we introduce a dynamics-informed imputation framework, termed Full-Partial Reconstruction Mapping (FPRM). In contrast to traditional approaches that directly fit time series interdependences, the FPRM embeds intrinsic dynamical priors via state-space reconstruction and recovers multiple incomplete series by learning diffeomorphic topology between attractors from complete and incomplete data. We validate the FPRM on paradigmatic model systems (e.g., an ecology system, the ordinary Lorenz system, a coupled 120-dimensional (120D) Lorenz system, and a coupled 120D Rössler system and real-world datasets (e.g., road occupancy rate from transportation system, electroencephalogram (EEG) signals from neuroscience, exchange rates from finance, and wind speed from climate systems). Even in high-dimensional systems where only one variable is fully observed and all others suffer from extreme missingness (e.g., 90%), the FPRM enables reliable imputation of multiple incomplete variables-a task that challenges most existing approaches. This dynamics-guided framework outperforms traditional approaches, alleviating substantial data gaps and enabling robust data-driven paradigms for complex dynamical systems.

papers.title: Will this sleep-disorder drug be the next big blockbuster?
The association of gout flare resolution with physical activity and sleep: a prospective remote-monitoring study.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to determine whether gout flare resolution is associated with physical activity and sleep. These findings were intended to inform the future development of a definition for flare resolution. Data from 81 participants with gout who experienced >1 flare during a 6-month prospective observational study were included. Daily activity (step count) and sleep (total sleep time and deep sleep percentage) were collected remotely using wrist-worn trackers. Daily flare occurrence was captured using smartphone diaries. Activity/sleep outcomes during each flare episode were compared to those during three resolution timeframes: T1: the first day following the flare; T2: the consecutive window immediately following the flare and equal in length to the flare; and T3: the consecutive window equal in length to the flare and immediately following a washout window (equal in length to the flare). Adjusted differences in medians between flare and resolution timeframes were estimated using linear quantile mixed models. Daily step count was lower during flares compared with all resolution timeframes (all P<0.033). T3 provided the best overall model fit, suggesting that resolution is most clearly distinguished from the flare when using this timeframe. No significant differences between flare and resolution were observed for the sleep outcomes for any resolution timeframe. Physical activity improves soon after flare cessation, with the clearest distinction between flare and resolution observed over a longer post-flare recovery period, whereas sleep metrics do not differentiate flare from resolution states. These findings support physical activity as a useful objective domain for gout flare resolution.

papers.title: An insular-orbitofrontal pathway supporting awareness of respiratory effort.
papers.abstract: In a recent study using human intracranial EEG recordings during inspiratory loading, Assi and colleagues identified parallel pathways for respiratory compensation and awareness. The anterior insula signals a neuromechanical mismatch to the orbitofrontal cortex for conscious appraisal, while high-frequency insular-frontal coupling enables ventilatory adjustments. The findings are highly relevant for disorders of altered respiratory perception.

papers.title: Buy one sleep therapy, get one free: potential benefits of better breathing for your bed partner.
A systematic review and meta-analysis of multi-health behavior interventions to reduce common mental health symptoms in people living with and beyond cancer.
papers.abstract: People living with and beyond cancer often report lower levels of physical activity, poorer sleep, and poorer diet quality, all of which may contribute to an increased risk of common mental health symptoms. This systematic review aimed to investigate the effects of multi-health behavior interventions designed to reduce common mental health symptoms in people living with and beyond cancer. This systematic review and meta-analyses followed PRISMA guidelines. The search, conducted up to July 2, 2025, included PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, PsycInfo, and PsyAPA, and grey literature. Multi-health behavior interventions (randomized and non-randomized trials) for people living with and beyond cancer, that targeted at least two behaviors (physical activity, diet, sleep, mindfulness) and assessed effects on common mental health outcomes (depression, anxiety, stress) were included. A total of 22 studies (n = 2,191 participants, 77.5% female; mean age 55 years) were included. Multi-health behavior interventions demonstrated small but significant improvements in depression (g = 0.40, 95% CI [0.26,0.55], p < 0.001), anxiety (g = 0.33, 95% CI [0.22,0.45], p < 0.001), and stress (g = 0.26, 95% CI [0.09,0.43], p = 0.003). Effects were consistent across treatment phases, cancer types, intervention type (flexible interventions and structured programs), number of intervention components, and intervention duration, with all subgroups showing significant improvements in at least one mental health outcome. Multi-health behavior interventions are associated with small but significant improvements in common mental health symptoms among people living with and beyond cancer. However, given the limitations and variable certainty of the available evidence, further high-quality RCTs are needed to confirm these findings.

papers.title: Nuclear Receptor Subfamily 1 Group D Member 1 Promotes Wound Healing in Diabetic Mice through Transcriptional Repression of Stimulator of Interferon Genes.
papers.abstract: Diabetic foot ulcer is one of the most debilitating complications of diabetes mellitus, primarily driven by persistent inflammation and impaired angiogenesis. This study investigates the role of the circadian clock protein, nuclear receptor subfamily 1 group D member 1 (NR1D1), in diabetic wound healing and elucidates its underlying mechanism. Clinical and experimental analyses revealed that NR1D1 levels were significantly reduced in both the serum and cutaneous wounds of diabetic patients and mice, with down-regulated NR1D1 correlating with delayed wound closure. Functionally, NR1D1 knockout markedly exacerbated wound healing impairment in diabetic mice, accompanied by elevated proinflammatory cytokines and dysfunctional angiogenesis. Conversely, NR1D1 overexpression suppressed IL-6 and IL-1β expression and rescued high-glucose-induced vascularization deficits in vitro. Additionally, diminished NR1D1 expression coincided with hyperactivated stimulator of interferon genes (STING) signaling in both diabetic skin wounds and high-glucose-treated human umbilical vein endothelial cells. Luciferase assays confirmed that NR1D1 directly represses human STING promoter activity. Taken together, the results indicated that NR1D1 deficiency severely deteriorates wound healing by provoking inflammation and dysregulating endothelial angiogenesis, which is driven by the high-glucose-triggered derepression of NR1D1-mediated transcriptional silencing of STING.

papers.title: Association between the triglyceride-glucose-waist circumference index and obstructive sleep apnoea: a hospital-based case-control study in China and the development of machine learning models.
Effect of Sleep Hygiene on Metabolic Syndrome in an Adult Rural Population in India: Protocol for a Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: Metabolic syndrome (MetS) refers to a group of conditions including high blood pressure, excess weight, high blood glucose, and abnormal cholesterol and triglyceride levels that together substantially increase the risk of heart disease and diabetes. Poor sleep hygiene is associated with a higher likelihood of type 2 diabetes, while sleep duration can affect the development of various MetS components. Approximately 25% of adults worldwide currently have MetS, and this prevalence is projected to increase to 50% by 2035. However, there is a distinct lack of evidence about the specific impact of sleep hygiene on cardiometabolic health within the rural Indian population. This study will focus on addressing this literature gap by evaluating these risk factor associations by using validated tools to help develop targeted community interventions. This study aims to estimate the prevalence of poor sleep quality and cardiometabolic risk factors in a rural Indian population and to determine the association between sleep hygiene and cardiometabolic risk factors. This study will be a community-based, cross-sectional, analytical study, and data collection will be carried out by trained personnel using validated tools during house-to-house visits. In this cross-sectional study of 281 rural Indian adults aged ≥40 years, sleep quality will be assessed via the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (a score >5 indicates poor sleep), alongside direct measurements of blood pressure, fasting plasma glucose, BMI (≥25 kg/m² for obesity), waist circumference, and the Madras Diabetes Research Foundation-Indian Diabetes Risk Score for diabetes risk. Data will be collected through a door-to-door approach, with informed consent entered into Google Forms, and quality checked via training and regular reviews. Using R software, analyses will include prevalence estimates with 95% CIs; chi-square or t tests for associations between poor sleep and cardiometabolic risks; and logistic regression (P<.05) adjusted for confounders such as diet, stress, and physical activity. This study began in January 2025 with conceptualization and ethics approval obtained in June 2025. Data collection commenced in August 2025 following Clinical Trial Registry-India registration, with 53 participants enrolled as of May 5, 2026. Standardized tools (GAD-7, PHQ-9, and GPAQ) were incorporated to assess key confounding variables. Data collection is projected to finish by January 2027, with final analysis and study conclusion expected by March 2027. The relationship between MetS and sleep hygiene warrants greater attention, particularly as poor sleep habits become increasingly prevalent alongside MetS. This study will deepen the understanding of their connection, paving the way for targeted interventions and prevention strategies. papers.title: Mobile EEG Reveals Age-Dependent Cognitive-Motor Interference with Increasing Motor Task Complexity- a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: This study examined age-related differences in behavior and brain dynamics underlying cognitive-motor interference (CMI) during motor dual-tasks (DT) with increasing motor task complexity. Behavioral performance and electrocortical activity were assessed in 19 younger adults (11 males, 8 females; 25.5 ± 2.3 years) and 11 older adults (6 males, 5 females; 72.6 ± 4.6 years) using mobile electroencephalography (EEG). Participants performed an oddball choice-reaction task under three conditions: sitting, standing, and treadmill walking. Event-related potential (ERPs; P1, N1, P3) amplitudes and latencies, response times, postural sway, and gait parameters were recorded to evaluate CMI. Data were analyzed using repeated-measures ANOVAs with within-subject factors of motor condition and stimulus type and age group as a between-subject factor. Older adults exhibited reduced step length compared to younger adults, but no DT-related changes in gait or postural sway were observed. Response times were generally slower in older adults and increased from sitting to standing and walking whereas younger adults showed slowing only from sitting to standing. Early sensory ERP components (P1, N1) demonstrated increased amplitudes with higher motor demands. The P3 component was reduced in amplitude in both groups during walking, with delayed latencies in older adults. For both groups, P3 latencies were associated with prolonged response times. Our findings suggest that this slowing during walking reflects altered cognitive resource allocation, characterized by delayed central information processing and enhanced early visual processing, rather than impaired peripheral motor coordination.

papers.title: Intrinsic and extrinsic connectivity of the seizure onset zone at rest and during stimulation.
papers.abstract: About half of patients who undergo epilepsy surgery for drug-resistant epilepsy have seizure recurrence, supporting the need for approaches that more accurately identify the epileptogenic zone, defined as the brain areas whose removal causes cessation of seizures. Altered network connectivity has emerged as a candidate biomarker of the epileptogenic zone, but how connectivity is altered in the epileptogenic zone remains uncertain, with prior studies reporting inconsistent results. We hypothesized that a difference in intrinsic versus extrinsic connectivity of the epileptogenic zone may explain prior discrepant findings. We retrospectively studied a multicenter cohort of 37 adult and 42 pediatric patients who underwent intracranial EEG recording and brain stimulation as part of epilepsy surgery planning. We measured spontaneous connectivity using Pearson correlation and perturbational connectivity using stimulation evoked potentials, modeling the connectivity according to the location of contacts in relation to the seizure onset zone while controlling for inter-electrode distance. For both adult and pediatric patients, resting connectivity was higher within compared to outside the seizure onset zone. However, resting connectivity between channels within and outside seizure onset zone was reduced. Stimulation connectivity followed a similar pattern, with elevated connectivity within the seizure onset zone but reduced connectivity from within to outside seizure onset zone. These results support the hypothesis that the seizure onset zone is disconnected from the rest of the brain but intrinsically hyperconnected. This result helps reconcile prior inconsistencies across studies, aligns with basic science studies, and suggests an approach for future translational work aiming to localize the epileptogenic zone.

papers.title: Dyspnea during resting breathing and carbon dioxide rebreathing in adult patients with congenital central hypoventilation syndrome.
papers.abstract: Congenital central hypoventilation syndrome (CCHS) is an ultra-rare genetic disorder caused by PHOX2B mutations. Patients lack central CO2 chemosensitivity and require ventilatory support during sleep. Children with CCHS have been reported to lack CO2-induced air hunger, but respiratory sensations and dyspnea have not been characterized in adults. Do genetically characterized adult CCHS patients experience respiratory sensations and dyspnea during unassisted resting breathing and CO2 rebreathing, and along which dimensions? This was a prospective controlled observational study conducted on a convenience sample derived from a national cohort of an ultrarare disease. Thirteen adult CCHS patients carrying PHOX2B mutations underwent Multidimensional Dyspnea Profile (MDP) assessment during unassisted resting breathing and at the end of CO2 rebreathing. Healthy controls were studied under the same conditions. Before the study, none of the patients had spontaneously reported dyspnea or bothersome respiratory sensations. When prompted with the MDP during resting breathing, 9/13 patients described breathing unpleasantness (non-zero MDP-A1) versus 0/18 controls (p < 0.0001), and 12/13 fulfilled criteria for dyspnea defined as breathing awareness associated with negative affect. During CO2 rebreathing, ventilatory responses remained profoundly blunted, yet breathing unpleasantness increased. Compared with controls, patients had lower sensory and affective ratings, with less frequent air hunger (p = 0.0108). MDP ratings did not correlate with ventilatory response to CO2 or genotype. Adult CCHS patients can experience conscious unpleasant breathing awareness at rest and retain a perceptual response to CO2 despite abolished or nearly abolished central chemosensitivity. These findings suggest respiratory interoceptive pathways beyond canonical brainstem chemosensitive circuits and support active multidimensional assessment of dyspnea in adult CCHS patients.

papers.title: Association between burst-suppression with identical bursts and multimodal measures of cerebral oxygenation after cardiac arrest.
papers.abstract: Burst-suppression with identical bursts (BSIB) is an electroencephalographic (EEG) pattern associated with severe post-cardiac arrest brain injury (PCABI). Whether modifiable mechanisms of brain injury underlie BSIB is unknown. We hypothesized BSIB is associated with impaired cerebral oxygen metabolism, reflected as pathologically elevated jugular bulb venous oxygen saturation (SjvO2), higher brain tissue oxygen tension (PbtO2), normal jugular bulb venous-to-arterial carbon dioxide gradient (PbCO2 gap, and lower intracranial pressure (ICP) compared to other EEG patterns. This single-center retrospective study included patients resuscitated from cardiac arrest who underwent EEG and SjvO2 or PbtO2 monitoring. We categorized EEG patterns as BSIB, malignant without BSIB, and non-malignant. Using mixed effects linear regression, we examined associations between EEG and SjvO2, PbCO2 gap, PbtO2, and ICP. The SjvO2 and PbtO2 cohorts included 109 and 33 patients, respectively. SjvO2 did not differ between BSIB and malignant EEGs (β=3; 95% CI, -0.6 to 7.0), butwas higher with BSIB compared to non-malignant patterns (β=12; 95% CI, 7.0 to 16.0). BSIB was associated with lower PbCO2 gap compared to malignant (β=-1.4; 95% CI, -2.6 to -0.3) and non-malignant (β=-2.6; 95% CI, -4.1 to -1.0) patterns. PbtO2 was highest with BSIB, but not significantly higher compared to malignant patterns in our adjusted model (β=4.0; 95% CI, -4.7 to 13.0). ICP was lower in those with BSIB compared to malignant patterns (β=-19.0; 95% CI, -32.5 to -5.6). Interpretation BSIB may represent a distinct subtype of PCABI characterized by impaired oxygen metabolism with preserved oxygen delivery and diffusion.

papers.title: Preoperative sleep deprivation prolongs postoperative hyperalgesia by downregulating spinal cord D2R expression via the PP2A/AKT-dependent NMDA receptor phosphorylation.
papers.abstract: Preoperative sleep deprivation (SD) is known to exacerbate postoperative pain, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Using a male mouse model of 48-hour continuous SD followed by incisional surgery, we found that SD alone induced transient mechanical hyperalgesia, and when combined with surgery (SI group) it significantly aggravated and prolonged postoperative pain recovery until day 10. On postoperative day 7, SI mice showed marked downregulation of spinal dopamine D2 receptor (D2R) expression and decreased spinal dopamine concentration. D2R was predominantly expressed on spinal glutamatergic neurons. Overexpression of D2R on these neurons via intrathecal AAV injection effectively alleviated the prolonged hyperalgesia, normalizing pain sensitivity by day 7. Mechanistically, D2R downregulation led to increased phosphorylation of NMDA receptor subunits (p-NR1 and p-NR2B) without altering total NMDA receptor levels. Co-immunoprecipitation revealed an interaction between D2R and protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A). SI mice exhibited decreased PP2A expression but increased p-AKT, p-GSK3β, and β-catenin, indicating activation of the PP2A/AKT signaling pathway, which were reversed by D2R overexpression. Furthermore, pharmacological activation of PP2A with DT-061 not only downregulated p-AKT, p-GSK3β, β-catenin, p-NR1 and p-NR2B, but also produced significant analgesia in SI mice. Collectively, these results demonstrate that preoperative sleep deprivation prolongs postoperative hyperalgesia by downregulating spinal D2R on glutamatergic neurons, which disinhibits the PP2A/AKT pathway and enhances NMDA receptor phosphorylation. Targeting D2R or its downstream PP2A/AKT signaling may represent a novel therapeutic strategy for managing persistent postoperative pain caused by preoperative sleep deprivation in male mice.

papers.title: Clinical and genetic correlates of a circadian subtype of depression in the Australian Genetics of Depression Study.
papers.abstract: Although commonly accepted depressive subtypes reflect phenotypic differences, there has been minimal progress in identification of discrete pathophysiological pathways, biomarkers or differential therapeutic approaches to effectively guide clinical management. To test the biological validity and clinical utility of a circadian subtype of depression on the basis of clinical course, differential medication response (self-reported) and genetic risk profile. Cross-sectional data were drawn from the nationwide Australian Genetics of Depression Study. Participants were classified as having a 'circadian' or 'non-circadian' subtype of depression on the basis of meeting criteria for at least three binary circadian-associated features: social jetlag, seasonality, delayed sleep midpoint, evening chronotype, morning tiredness and hypersomnia. Clinical course characteristics were compared. Associations with response to commonly prescribed antidepressants and polygenic risk scores for mental disorders and sleep, circadian, metabolic and inflammatory traits were investigated using logistic regression models. A total of 2604 participants (23%; 80% female; mean age 37.87 ± 13.62 years) had a circadian subtype. They reported an earlier age at onset (P < 0.001), more severe clinical features including (hypo)manic-like and psychotic-like experiences, suicidality, psychological distress and somatic complaints (all P < 0.001), weight gain during depressive episodes (P < 0.001), poorer response to selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (odds ratio 0.88 [95% CI 0.82, 0.94]) and serotonin-noradrenaline reuptake inhibitors (odds ratio 0.89 [95% CI 0.83, 0.97]), and more side-effects compared with those with a non-circadian subtype. Having a circadian subtype was associated with higher polygenic risk scores for attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (odds ratio 1.11 [95% CI 1.06, 1.17]), major depression (odds ratio 1.11 [95% CI 1.06, 1.16]), anxiety (odds ratio 1.10 [95% CI 1.04, 1.15]), bipolar disorder (odds ratio 1.09 [95% CI 1.04, 1.14]), body mass index (odds ratio 1.09 [95% CI 1.05, 1.14]), triglycerides (odds ratio 1.10 [95% CI 1.06, 1.16]), interleukin-6 (odds ratio 1.08 [95% CI 1.03, 1.13]), higher insulin resistance (odds ratio 1.08 [95% CI 1.04, 1.13]), later sleep midpoint (odds ratio 1.15 [95% CI 1.10, 1.21]), insomnia (odds ratio 1.08 [95% CI 1.03, 1.13]) and later chronotype (odds ratio 0.68 [95% CI 0.65, 0.71]). These findings support the face validity and potential clinical utility of a circadian subtype of depression as a clinical profile. Pending independent replication, investigation of its biology and predictive utility are warranted.
papers.journal: The British journal of psychiatry : the journal of mental science

papers.title: An examination of the effect of dual task on gait in Parkinson's disease and REM sleep behavior disorder.
papers.abstract: Gait variability is a hallmark of Parkinson's disease (PD) and has been linked to cognitive deficits and fall risk. Rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder (RBD) is a strong predictor of synucleinopathies, yet evidence for gait changes in RBD is inconsistent. Performing a dual task increases gait variability, an effect that can be quantified using a cost function. Determine the degree to which dual task cost differs between control, RBD, and PD participants at baseline, and between RBD converters versus non-converters at follow-up. 46 RBD, 23 control, and 14 PD participants completed standardized gait analysis at baseline. Parameters chosen a priori for analysis included enhanced gait variability index (eGVI), functional ambulation performance (FAP), velocity, step length, cadence, base of support, and double support time. Medical records were surveilled for 3 years following participant enrollment, determining that 6 RBD participants converted to Parkinsonism. Baseline gait indices and dual task costs were compared between control, RBD, and PD groups at enrollment, and between RBD stable and RBD converters at follow-up. The PD group had greater eGVI, as well as greater dual task cost for FAP, cadence, width, and double support time. No differences in gait variability or cost were identified between RBD and control groups at baseline. Compared to the stable group, RBD converters had greater dual task cost for FAP, velocity, cadence, and double support time. Increases in dual task cost for specific gait parameters may identify RBD patients at imminent risk of phenoconversion.

papers.title: Apnea-hypopnea index-oxygen desaturation index (AHI-ODI) discordance in obstructive sleep apnea: association with symptom burden and cardiometabolic comorbidity: A retrospective cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: The apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) counts respiratory events but not the depth or duration of accompanying desaturation. We examined AHI-ODI discordance (AHI minus oxygen desaturation index, ODI) and its associations with daytime symptom burden and prevalent cardiometabolic comorbidity. Single-center retrospective cross-sectional study of 200 adults with OSA (January 2023-January 2025). Five indices (AHI, ODI, mean SpO2, T90 and AHI-ODI discordance) were examined; excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS; Epworth Sleepiness Scale ≥ 11) was the primary outcome. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, BMI and an AHI-ODI × sex interaction. The cohort was 77.5% male, median age 57 years (48.8-64.2). For EDS, AHI-ODI discordance showed the numerically highest AUC (0.639, p < 0.001), followed by T90 (0.627), and mean SpO2 and ODI (0.609 each); AHI was not significant (0.546, p = 0.264). No pairwise difference was significant. AHI-ODI discordance remained independently associated with EDS after adjustment (OR 1.04 per event/h, 95% CI 1.01-1.07, p = 0.008), with no significant sex interaction. Among secondary outcomes, T90 showed the highest AUCs for diabetes mellitus (0.644) and hypertension (0.615), and mean SpO2 for heart failure (0.608). No index discriminated against previous stroke or atrial fibrillation. AHI-ODI discordance was independently, but only modestly, associated with EDS, whereas oxygenation indices were related to prevalent cardiometabolic comorbidity. The discrimination was insufficient, and all reported cut-offs are exploratory. AHI-ODI discordance is not a measure of sleep apnea-specific hypoxic burden.

papers.title: The spatial extent of fast ripples is associated with cognitive and language deficits in children with focal epilepsy: An exploratory SEEG study.
papers.abstract: To determine if the spatial extent of interictal fast ripples in focal epilepsy patients is associated with brain dysfunction. Thirty pediatric focal epilepsy patients who underwent SEEG investigation had their cognitive and language deficits assessed in scales of 0 to 4. Fast ripples (250-500 Hz), ripples (80-250 Hz), and IEDs were automatically detected in 10 min during NREM sleep. We fitted linear models to the relationship between the cognitive deficit scale and the spatial spread of the interictal neurophysiologic events (number of channels with rate of events > 10 % of maximum rate). For the language deficit, we computed the Spearman correlation between the median rate of events in all brain regions and the deficit scale. Cognitive deficit scale was significantly associated with the number of channels with fast ripples (p = 0.049), not so with ripples (p = 0.31), IEDs (p = 0.31). The potential confound of number of explored channels did not improve the fitting of the models. Language deficits were not correlated with the number of channels showing interictal events. However, from all brain regions the most statistically significant correlations (p < 0.01) were between median fast ripple rates in the left and right pars opercularis and triangularis of the inferior frontal gyrus (Broca's area and its contralateral counterpart) with r = 0.66, p = 0.003 (18 patients), in the superior temporal gyrus in the language dominant hemisphere with r = 0.72, p = 0.005 (13 patients), and the dominant basal temporal region with r = 0.79, p = 0.006 (10 patients). Median rates of IEDs and ripples exhibited lower correlation with language deficits in these regions. Widespread fast ripples are associated with increased cognitive deficits, and language deficiencies are correlated with fast ripple rates in brain regions associated with language. The extent of fast-ripple activity was associated with cognitive deficit severity in this cohort, whereas the corresponding associations for ripples and IEDs did not reach statistical significance.

papers.title: Caregiver experience of diazepam nasal spray treatment in children aged 2-5 years.
papers.abstract: Caregiving for young children with epilepsy (CWE) may have a large impact on families that extends beyond medical care (e.g., psychological conditions and financial concerns). Epilepsy requires long-term treatment, which may include medications both for daily and urgent use. Diazepam nasal spray was used for acute seizure episodes in CWE aged 2-5 years and was evaluated in a Phase 1/2a pharmacokinetics (PK) and safety study. Caregivers provided assessments of changes in their children's responses to treatment and their own experience of treatment usefulness. CWE aged 2-5 y were enrolled in an open-label PK study of diazepam nasal spray with a 180-day open-label safety period and an optional extension period. Data from a seizure severity questionnaire and a caregiver survey at baseline and at safety period follow-up visits (days 30, 90, and 180) were included. Of 36 enrolled patients, 35 entered, and 31 completed the safety period; 27 entered and completed the optional extension period. Caregivers reported improvement in seizure recovery (61.5% at day 180 vs 38.5% at baseline), indicating it did not take a while for patients to recover after seizures. Similarly, caregivers reported improvements at day 180, compared with baseline, with reductions in caregiver worry (51.9%) and sleep disturbance (57.7%). Caregivers reported much milder and fewer seizure clusters at day 180 vs baseline (50.0%), and family improvement with treatment (69.2%). Caregivers of CWE aged 2-5 years treated with diazepam nasal spray reported improvement in seizure episodes and daily function, reinforcing the value of appropriate treatment.

papers.title: Generalized Spike-Wave discharges and myoclonic features in a subgroup of children with Self-Limited epilepsy with centrotemporal spikes.
papers.abstract: Generalized spike-wave discharges (GSWD) are occasionally observed in patients with self-limited epilepsy with centrotemporal spikes (SeLECTS), but their clinical significance remains unclear. This study aimed to characterize the electroclinical features of these patients and to explore their potential clinical implications. We retrospectively reviewed the clinical data of 148 children diagnosed with SeLECTS at Xuanwu Hospital from June 2015 to October 2025. Patients with GSWD on electroencephalography were identified and compared with those without GSWD regarding demographic characteristics, seizure semiology, auxiliary examination findings, treatment response, and outcomes. GSWD were identified in 9 of 148 patients (6.1 %) with SeLECTS. These 9 patients included 4 males and 5 females, with a median onset age of 8 (IQR: 5-10) years. Compared with those without GSWD, they more frequently showed wakefulness seizures (44.4 % vs 5.8 %, p < 0.05), generalized tonic-clonic seizures during sleep (44.4 %), and myoclonic manifestations (77.8 %). Other clinical variables were similar between groups. All 9 patients achieved freedom from focal and generalized tonic-clonic seizures, though one required prolonged combination therapy. Two patients with follow-up exceeding 10 years showed electroclinical evolution toward juvenile myoclonic epilepsy, characterized by the absence of centrotemporal spikes, with generalized spike-wave bursts recurring on later EEGs. We identified a subgroup of patients with SeLECTS characterized by the coexistence of GSWD and myoclonic features, showing partial electroclinical overlap with juvenile myoclonic epilepsy. These findings broaden the electroclinical spectrum of SeLECTS, though the relationship between focal and generalized network dysfunction in this subgroup requires confirmation in larger, prospectively followed cohorts.

papers.title: The development and validation of the pre-sleep excitement-inducing activities scale.
papers.abstract: Existing pre-sleep arousal measures emphasize distress-based symptoms, leaving positively valenced sources of activation, such as excitement-inducing evening activities, largely unassessed and a potential unmeasured contributor to sleep-onset difficulty. We developed and evaluated the Pre-Sleep Excitement-Inducing Activities Scale (PSEIA) to address this gap. A 34-item pool underwent expert review and cognitive debriefing. Exploratory factor analysis (EFA) was conducted in Phase 1 (n = 150). In an independent Phase 2 sample (n = 301), confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) tested correlated three-factor, higher-order, and bifactor models. Internal consistency, two-week test-retest reliability (n = 150), and associations with the Pre-Sleep Arousal Scale (PSAS) were evaluated. Although parallel analysis suggested four factors, a more interpretable three-factor solution retained 18 items: Cognitive Stimulation, Informational Stimulation, and Recreational Stimulation. The correlated three-factor model showed CFI = .99, TLI = .99, RMSEA = .08, and SRMR = .06. The higher-order model had identical global fit; the bifactor model showed CFI = .99, TLI = .99, RMSEA = .07, and SRMR = .05. Total-score reliability was high (α = .92; ω = .95; ωH = .74), as was test-retest reliability (ICC = .93). The PSEIA correlated moderately with PSAS total score (r = .51, p < .001). The two shorter factors showed substantial overlap, and the three-item factor had marginal alpha (.69). The PSEIA provides an initial measure of activity-linked pre-sleep activation. Its reliable total score is supported by shared variance across factors, but subscale distinctiveness and clinical utility require further validation.

papers.title: Characteristics of Patients With Epileptic Spasm Onset Over 2 Years of Age.
papers.abstract: The definition of late-onset epileptic spasms has shifted from epileptic spasm (ES) onset over one-2 years of age, due to the emergence of infantile epileptic spasms syndrome. This study investigated differences in clinical characteristics between patients who demonstrated ES at one-2 years of age versus >2 years of age. This retrospective study included patients aged ≥one year who developed ES and visited Saitama Children's Medical Center between January 1, 1990, and March 31, 2023. Patients were classified based on age at ES onset into the one-2-year-old group (one-2 years group) and the older-than-2-year-old group (≥2 years group). The clinical characteristics of each group and the differences in clinical characteristics between the two groups were investigated. The one-2 years group included 10 patients, while the ≥2 years group comprised 8 patients. Comparison between the two groups revealed that the ≥2-year group exhibited higher developmental quotient at ES onset, longer lead time, and more misdiagnosis, and less hypsarrhythmia on interictal electroencephalography. At the last follow-up, intellectual disability (ID) was present in all patients across both cohorts. Regarding the severity distribution of ID, higher proportion of patients in the ≥2 years group demonstrated mild ID and a lower proportion demonstrated severe ID compared to those in the one-2 years group. Age at ES onset may reflect different clinical phenotypes and outcomes within the late-onset spectrum.

papers.title: Clinical Hypnosis for Chronic Non-Cancer Pain: A Scoping Review.
papers.abstract: Chronic non-cancer pain requires multimodal management, and clinical hypnosis has been examined as a complementary intervention. This PRISMA ScR scoping review mapped the extent and characteristics of the evidence base, intervention features, and research gaps for clinical hypnosis in chronic non-cancer pain. We included 48 intervention studies involving 3,166 participants, encompassing randomized controlled trials and other study designs. Hypnosis was applied to nociceptive, neuropathic, nociplastic, and mixed pain presentations using diverse techniques and delivery formats. Outcomes most frequently included pain intensity and pain related distress, with additional measures of coping, sleep, and daily functioning. The mapped literature commonly involved small samples, frequent use of passive comparators, limited demographic reporting and diversity, and variable intervention reporting. This review extends prior syntheses by detailing how clinical hypnosis has been operationalized for chronic non-cancer pain and by identifying methodological and reporting gaps to guide future research.
papers.journal: The International journal of clinical and experimental hypnosis

papers.title: Quantitative Analysis of Electroencephalography in Hypnosis: A Neurophysiological Approach.
papers.abstract: Hypnosis is a unique state of consciousness marked by heightened response to suggestions, focused attention, and altered cognitive control. This article explores the neural connections involved in hypnosis through electroencephalography (EEG) studies, examining brain changes during hypnosis and their relationship to hypnotic depth and susceptibility. Theta waves, linked to hypnotic depth, are stronger in highly hypnotizable individuals, while gamma waves are associated with focus, suggestion acceptance, and emotional responses. Hypnosis also induces frequency-dependent reorganization of large-scale brain connectivity, particularly in frontal-parietal and attentional networks, enhancing subjective experiences and responsiveness. EEG patterns reveal more dynamic neural activity during hypnosis, which cannot be captured by linear metrics alone. Hemispheric analysis shows greater left-hemisphere activity in highly hypnotizable individuals, particularly in emotionally and verbally mediated tasks, challenging the right-hemisphere dominance model. Event related potential (ERP) findings show that hypnosis affects information processing at both pre-attentional and cognitive levels. These insights contribute to understanding hypnosis' impact on the brain and its potential for personalized therapeutic interventions.

papers.title: Comment on Martyn-Nemeth et al. Sleep Optimization to Improve Glycemic Targets in Adults With Type 1 Diabetes: A Randomized Controlled Parallel Intervention Trial.
Modification of locomotion-respiration coupling in patients with obstructive sleep apnea syndrome.
papers.abstract: Locomotion is a complex motor task integrating sensory-motor and cognitive inputs through central pattern generator control. Locomotion-respiration coupling (LRC), defined as the synchronization between gait and breathing events, has been described during running and walking. Patients with obstructive sleep apnea syndrome (OSAS) exhibit altered gait patterns during wakefulness, which appear to be partially independent of nocturnal symptomatic treatment. While intermittent hypoxia may induce long-term ("fixed") central nervous system alterations, OSAS patients also display "reversible" adaptive mechanisms during wakefulness aimed at preventing upper airway (UA) collapse, involving changes in respiratory control and posture. Whether these adaptive mechanisms affect LRC and contribute to gait alterations remains unknown. Ten awake patients with controlled OSAS treated with a mandibular advancement device (MAD) and ten matched healthy controls performed a one-minute walking trial on an instrumented treadmill with motion capture. Ventilation was assessed via thoracic expansion, and spatiotemporal gait parameters were extracted from kinematic and force platform data. LRC was quantified using phase-locking values (PLV) between ventilatory events and sagittal-plane joint kinematics. OSAS patients were assessed both with and without their MAD. Compared with controls, OSAS patients exhibited a longer double-stance phase and a shorter swing phase. Expiratory events occurred preferentially during double stance in OSAS patients, whereas controls showed a higher occurrence during swing. PLV analysis revealed increased synchronization between inspiratory events and hip and knee motion, as well as between expiratory events and trunk and hip motion in OSAS patients. These significative differences were no longer observed when patients wore their MAD. Logistic regression demonstrated that PLV metrics of inspiratory-hip and expiratory-trunk coupling effectively discriminated OSAS patients from controls, but not when UA stabilization was applied. Awake patients with controlled OSAS exhibit altered gait patterns characterized by increased locomotion-respiration coupling. This heightened synchronization likely reflects adaptive, reversible strategies aimed at limiting UA collapsibility during wakefulness rather than fixed hypoxia-related impairments alone. LRC may represent a functional marker of daytime motor alterations in OSAS and a potential target for interventions addressing UA mechanics beyond nocturnal treatment.

papers.title: Type 1 diabetes in the youngest: from distinct needs to new frontiers in care.
papers.abstract: Type 1 diabetes (T1D) in very young children poses unique clinical and psychosocial challenges due to distinct physiological, developmental, and behavioural characteristics of this age group. Advances in diabetes technology, particularly hybrid closed-loop (HCL) systems, are transforming T1D management in young children by integrating continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) with automated insulin delivery (AID). Evidence from randomized controlled trials and real-world studies consistently demonstrates that HCL systems improve time in range, lower HbA1c, and reduce glycaemic variability without increasing the risk of severe hypoglycaemia or diabetic ketoacidosis. Benefits are especially evident overnight, when glycaemic control is more stable, although daytime management remains more complex, due to unpredictable behaviours typical of preschoolers and marked circadian variability in insulin needs. Accordingly, the use of HCL fail to decrease hypoglycaemia in this population. Additional strategies, such as insulin dilution, may facilitate safer delivery of small doses, reducing the risk of nocturnal hypoglycaemia and improving time in range (TIR). Beyond metabolic outcomes, HCL systems substantially improve quality of life for both children and caregivers, reducing fear of hypoglycaemia, easing parental burden, and improving sleep and emotional well-being. Overall, current evidence supports HCL as a safe and effective therapeutic option for very young children with T1D, offering significant metabolic and psychosocial benefits, without completely eliminating the risk of hypoglycaemia. These findings highlight the need for further refinement of age-specific algorithms capable of addressing the unique physiological variability of this population.

papers.title: A comparison of clinical and procedural outcomes of transforaminal versus parasagittal interlaminar epidural steroid injections for radicular pain secondary to lumbar disc herniation.
papers.abstract: This study aims to compare the clinical and procedural outcomes of transforaminal epidural steroid injections (TFESIs) and parasagittal interlaminar epidural steroid injections (P-ILESIs) in patients with unilateral radicular pain secondary to lumbar disc herniation (LDH). Between January 2024 and June 2025, a total of 162 patients with unilateral radicular pain caused by single-level LDH were included in this retrospective, observational cohort study. The patients were divided into the two groups based on the technique as the TFESI group (n = 82) and the P-ILESI group (n = 80). Pain, disability, sleep quality, and health-related quality of life were assessed using the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS), Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and Short Form-12 (SF-12), respectively at baseline, one month, and six months. Fluoroscopy time and cumulative radiation dose were also recorded. Of the patients, 120 were male and 42 were female with a median age of 47 (range 22 to 65) years. Both techniques significantly improved pain, disability, sleep quality, and quality of life at one and six months (p < 0.001). The reduction in NRS from baseline was greater with TFESI at one month (p = 0.008), but not at six months (p = 0.545). The ODI scores were lower with TFESI at one month, although the magnitude of improvement from baseline did not significantly differ and no difference was observed at six months. Quality of life outcomes were comparable between the groups. The P-ILESI required longer fluoroscopy time and higher radiation exposure than TFESI (p < 0.001 for both). No major complications occurred, and minor adverse events were infrequent and comparable between the groups (p = 0.764). Both TFESI and P-ILESI appear to be effective and safe approaches for the treatment of radicular pain associated with LDH. The choice of epidural approach should be individualized according to clinical and anatomical considerations, as well as operator experience.
