papers.title: Advanced Detection of Pre-Ictal Stages in Epilepsy Using Convolutional Neural Networks and Automated Feature Extraction.
papers.abstract: During a seizure, the neurons in the brain are firing abnormally. It is important to identify the symptoms to stop the spread of the virus, as a late diagnosis greatly increases the risk of infecting others. The domain is still heavily biased towards the use of just a few publicly available scalp EEG datasets (for instance, CHB/MIT) and has barely scratched the surface in relation to the use of iEEGs with little consideration for multi-centre or private datasets. Class imbalance, where preictals outnumber interictals and icts, also presents a challenge in the training process due to the non-stationarity, variability, and presence of noise in the EEG data. The study used the pre-processed data and the convolution neural network model to predict the duration of the pre-ictal phase of an epilepsy attack. To this end, the CHB-MIT gathering dataset is used. Hand-crafted features usually work with conventional methods. The suggested approach comprises signal metadata processing, an automatic feature extraction tool supported by signal characteristic identification and LSTM and SVM-based result classification. The proposed model defines the pre-ictal state considering sensitivity and specificity. Initially the detection system was configured for a two-second window duration.

papers.title: Beyond the pump: a narrative review of the acute molecular, metabolic, and neuropsychological responses to a bout of resistance exercise.
papers.abstract: Resistance training is widely recognized for its chronic adaptations, including strength, muscle hypertrophy, and improvements in musculoskeletal health. However, a single bout of resistance exercise also elicits a range of acute physiological and psychological responses across multiple systems. These immediate responses have generally been examined within individual physiological domains, with less attention given to their coexistence and temporal overlap following a single session. This narrative review synthesizes evidence relating to the acute systemic effects of a single bout of resistance exercise. Literature was identified through iterative searches of electronic databases and reference lists, with emphasis on primary human studies directly examining acute responses, alongside relevant systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and mechanistic literature. Acute resistance exercise induces responses across endocrine and myokine, metabolic, vascular, pain-related, psychological, cognitive, and sleep-related domains. Contracting skeletal muscle releases myokines and other signalling molecules with potential systemic actions. Post-exercise energy expenditure and muscle protein synthesis may remain elevated during recovery, while glucose uptake and insulin sensitivity are enhanced. Acute resistance exercise can also produce exercise-induced hypoalgesia, reduce state anxiety, improve aspects of executive function and cognitive performance, and may influence sleep continuity and neurophysiological activity. These responses differ in their evidential basis and physiological significance, encompassing directly observed short-term effects, proposed regulatory mechanisms, and more tentative hypotheses regarding longer-term implications. A single bout of resistance exercise produces temporally overlapping responses across multiple physiological and psychological systems. These responses should not be assumed to represent adaptive remodelling or direct mechanisms of chronic health benefit. Nevertheless, integrating them provides a broader perspective on the immediate multisystem consequences of resistance exercise and may help inform future research examining how repeated acute responses relate to longer-term adaptation and health outcomes.

papers.title: Persistent postoperative pediatric pain: a secondary analysis of the 4P prospective observational multicenter study.
papers.abstract: Few large studies have examined the prevalence and risk factors for persistent postoperative pain (PPOP) in children. Chronic pain in childhood can lead to significant personal suffering, including non-attendance at school and social isolation. In a prospective observational multicenter study, we followed 601 children undergoing common pediatric surgeries. This secondary analysis aimed to describe the prevalence, characteristics, and exploratory risk factor associations of PPOP. The primary outcome was defined as recurrent pain (4 on an age-specific scale lasting for over three months after surgery. Persistent pain was further characterized regarding its impact on various activities and whether it was anatomically localized at the site of surgery. Of the 601 children, 380 were available for follow-up at 3 and 6 months after surgery. The median age was 5 years, and 34% were female. Preoperative pain was reported by 41 children (11%), and 126 (33%) reported anxiety or sleep problems before surgery. Thirteen (3%) patients experienced PPOP (≥ 4) after either 3 (n = 9) or 6 months (n = 4). Ten attributed the pain to the surgical area, and in six children, the pain affected activity-levels. Five children used analgesics for their symptoms. Only one child experienced pain daily, and three children reported weekly pain. Applying a stricter definition from ICD-11 to our cohort resulted in an even lower PPOP prevalence: only three (0.8%) children experienced pain lasting more than 3 months, in whom the pain began or increased after surgery, was at a level ≥4, influenced activity-levels, and was located in the surgical area. The prevalence of persistent postoperative pain after common pediatric surgeries was very low. As one of the few prospective multicenter studies in this field, these findings are noteworthy.

papers.title: Acupotomy Alleviates Pain and Attenuates Spinal Neuronal Hyperexcitability in Knee Osteoarthritis Rats: Implication of the CaMKII/GluA1 Axis.
papers.abstract: To investigate the spinal mechanisms underlying the analgesic effects of acupotomy on chronic pain and central sensitization in rats with monosodium iodoacetate (MIA)-induced knee osteoarthritis (KOA). Following MIA-induced KOA and a three-week acupotomy intervention in rats, pain behaviors and joint pathology were assessed. Spinal RNA-sequencing was performed to identify differentially expressed genes. Key targets (CaMKII and GluA1) were validated at both mRNA and protein levels using RT-qPCR and Western blotting. Furthermore, immunofluorescence and whole-cell patch-clamp electrophysiology were employed to evaluate the activation and excitability of spinal substantia gelatinosa (SG) neurons. Acupotomy significantly alleviated mechanical and thermal hyperalgesia and reduced joint degeneration in KOA rats. RNA-seq analysis revealed the modulation of 220 genes in the spinal cord. These DEGs were significantly enriched in calcium signaling and synaptic transmission pathways, highlighting CaMKII and Gria1 as potential key molecules. Molecular validations confirmed that acupotomy downregulated CaMKII and Gria1 mRNA expression and the phosphorylation ratios of CaMKII and GluA1. Furthermore, acupotomy reduced the activation of p-CaMKII-positive neurons in the spinal SG region and dampened their abnormally high-frequency action potential discharges. Acupotomy intervention ameliorates peripheral joint degeneration and exerts significant analgesia in KOA, which is accompanied by a reduction in the intrinsic hyperexcitability of spinal SG neurons. Although direct causal validation utilizing targeted inhibitors is warranted, our findings suggest that this analgesic effect is closely associated with the downregulation of the CaMKII/GluA1 signaling axis, providing a plausible central mechanistic framework.

papers.title: EEG signature in psychiatrist's subjective experience: a pilot study.
papers.abstract: The Assessment of Clinician's Subjective Experience (ACSE) is a self-report questionnaire developed to evaluate clinicians' subjective experiences during patient interactions. While its psychometric properties and clinical validity have been supported, its neurobiological correlates have not yet been investigated. In this pilot study, two clinicians and ten patients participated in a three-phase protocol comprising: (1) a first clinical interview, (2) ACSE administration, and (3) listening to the audio recording of the first clinical interview. EEG activity was recorded from clinicians during both the first clinical interview and questionnaire administration. Neural data were analyzed in terms of relative power spectral density, node strength, and global efficiency computed from imaginary coherence. Clinicians were psychiatrists, one male and one female. Seven patients were diagnosed with mixed anxiety and depressive disorder, and three with unspecified anxiety disorders. ACSE scores were highest for the Difficulty in attunement and Engagement dimensions, consistent with previous literature. EEG findings revealed dimension-specific and topographically distinct oscillatory patterns for only two ACSE dimensions: Difficulty in Attunement and Engagement. More limited evidence emerged for Disconfirmation. Functional connectivity analyses indicated different network profiles, characterized by differences in global efficiency patterns. Correlational analyses further identified significant associations between ACSE dimensions and EEG-derived features. These preliminary findings provide initial evidence that clinicians' subjective experiences during clinical encounters could be associated with measurable neural signatures, offering a novel perspective on the neurobiological basis of intersubjective processes in clinical settings.

papers.title: A feature-optimized EEG framework using multiscale entropy and metaheuristic optimization for cognitive analysis.
papers.abstract: Cognitive activity plays an important role by influencing working-memory, problem-solving, attention, response and decision making. EEG serves as a non-invasive approach to analyze neural activity associated with cognitive processing. The current study aims to identify the more contributing features to analyze the cognitive activity between sports and non-sports groups. The present study included 100 participants, consisting of 80 males and 20 females aged between 19 and 23 years. EEG signals were acquired and preprocessed using filtering methods to remove unwanted noise and artifacts. The four-entropy metrics dispersion entropy, permutation entropy, sample entropy, and fuzzy entropy were applied to the coarse-graining method across multiple temporal scales to analyze the complexity of EEG signals. To identify the most informative feature subsets and reduce redundancy, filter-based methods such as Mutual Information, Pearson Correlation, Minimum Redundancy Maximum Relevance and wrapper-based methods such as Genetic Algorithm and Particle Swarm Optimization were applied. Finally for differentiating the cognitive activity, five machine learning classifiers that include Support Vector Machine, Artificial Neural Network, K-nearest neighbor, Decision Tree and Random Forest were applied. Statistical methods such as T-test and Fleiss kappa were used to analyse the performance efficiency. Feature extraction phase yielded a total of 160 multiscale entropy features. The entire features when fed into both filter-based and wrapper-based methods, Genetic Algorithm based optimization yielded a minimal contributing feature subset with high nested cross-validated accuracy of 93.0 ± 2.7% with Support Vector Machine. This contributing feature subset was used as input for five different machine learning classifiers for differentiating the cognitive activity between both groups. The five classifiers demonstrated high cross-validated agreement on held-out subjects, with a mean Fleiss' kappa of 0.874 ± 0.051 (95% CI: 0.811-0.937), depicting a good inter-classifier agreement for classification of samples into sports and non-sports individuals. The study demonstrates that multiscale entropy features combined with metaheuristic-based feature optimization can effectively analyze the cognitive activity between sports and non-sports individuals. The proposed EEG framework provides a structured approach for real-time cognitive activity analysis using compact and informative entropy-based feature subsets.

papers.title: Study protocol for microneurographic investigation of nociceptor sensitisation in fibromyalgia syndrome (MICRO-FMS).
papers.abstract: Chronic pain in fibromyalgia may be driven by abnormal ongoing activity in a subclass of C-fibre nociceptors known as Type1B or CMi nociceptors. As is common in C-nociceptor microneurography studies, the modest patient numbers in these prior studies generate large confidence intervals around the point estimate of the prevalence of this abnormal activity. This complicates the interpretation of the relative importance of this ongoing nociceptor activity as a pain generating mechanism in fibromyalgia. The study aims to improve precision via an adaptive Bayesian protocol that maximises the yield and quality of data collection whilst minimising patient burden. This study will clarify whether the prevalence of ongoing nociceptor activity is higher in the fibromyalgia patient population, and if this is correlated with their sensory phenotype and/or pain experience, providing much needed insight into the mechanisms of the condition. The study employs an optimised microneurography protocol with an adaptive study design. The microneurography protocol incorporates early identification of CMi nociceptors via an abbreviated activity dependent slowing protocol to increase yields enabling efficient collection of the primary outcome data. The adaptive study design will use Bayesian principles to iteratively assess the predictive probability of futility, and terminate early if there is high confidence that the hypothesis is false. Furthermore, the study will employ questionnaires to explore links with pain in the area under study to the electrophysiology data. Finally, quantitative sensory testing will be used to investigate whether the irritable nociceptor phenotype is associated with abnormalities in CMi nociceptor physiology. This study has received HRA REC approval in the UK. Participants will provide written informed consent, and may withdraw at any time without consequence. At the end of the study, the results will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publication, and the data made available via a data repository.

Sleep stage-specific heart rate variability feature-driven clustering analysis: identifying cardiac autonomic endotypes with long-term cardiovascular predictive value.
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular risk assessment in obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) has traditionally relied on the Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI). However, AHI primarily reflects respiratory event burden and may not adequately capture inter-individual heterogeneity in sleep-related cardiorespiratory regulation. This study aimed to identify sleep stage-specific heart rate variability (HRV) phenotypes and evaluate their associations with long-term cardiovascular outcomes. Data were obtained from the Sleep Heart Health Study (SHHS). After exclusion of participants with missing clinical covariates or outcome data, 4029 individuals were included. Linear and non-linear HRV features were extracted from stage-specific electrocardiographic segments during N2, N3, and rapid eye movement (REM) sleep. K-means clustering was performed independently for each sleep stage after Z-score standardization, and the optimal cluster number was determined using silhouette coefficients and the elbow method. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models and Kaplan-Meier analyses were used to evaluate associations between HRV-informed phenotypes and all-cause mortality, coronary heart disease, and cardiovascular disease (CVD). Three HRV-informed phenotypes were identified within the selected clustering framework across N2, N3, and REM sleep stages: Stable (Cluster 0), Burden (Cluster 1), and High risk (Cluster 2). Compared with the Stable phenotype, the High-risk phenotype was consistently associated with increased cardiovascular risk, with the strongest association observed for incident CVD in the N2 stage [hazard ratio (HR) 1.468, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.280-1.684, P < 0.001]. Similar associations were observed in the N3 (HR 1.426, 95% CI 1.249-1.629, P < 0.001) and REM (HR 1.394, 95% CI 1.216-1.598, P < 0.001) stages. Sequential adjustment for AHI, oxygen desaturation index, arousal index, and sleep efficiency resulted in only minimal attenuation of hazard estimates, indicating that the prognostic associations were largely independent of conventional respiratory severity measures. In contrast, the Burden phenotype was consistently associated with lower all-cause mortality across all three sleep stages (HR 0.83-0.85, all P < 0.001). Subgroup analyses stratified by OSA severity demonstrated broadly consistent prognostic associations across AHI strata. Incorporating sleep stage-specific HRV features into conventional clinical phenotyping provides complementary prognostic information beyond traditional respiratory severity metrics. HRV-informed phenotyping may improve long-term cardiovascular risk stratification in patients with OSA.

papers.title: Variable task difficulty with augmented sensory feedback for motor training in virtual reality.
papers.abstract: This study examined how motor task difficulty and augmented sensory feedback (ASF) modality influence task performance, physiological responses, and perceptual experience during virtual reality (VR)-based upper-limb motor training. Building on related brace- and VR-based ASF platforms previously examined in neurotypical and spinal cord injury cohorts, the long-term goal is to support neurorehabilitation-oriented adaptive VR training; however, the present study used neurotypical participants as an initial validation step. Fourteen right-handed neurotypical participants used a supportive upper-limb brace and surface electromyography (EMG) for myoelectric control of a virtual robotic arm in a two-dimensional tracking task. A 2 × 2 within-subject design crossed ASF modality (visual feedback versus visual + haptic feedback) with task difficulty (straight-line versus sinusoidal trajectory). Outcomes included normalized path length, task completion time, movement jerk, alpha- and beta-band electroencephalogram (EEG) power over motor cortex, heart rate, EMG amplitude, EMG-displacement-based virtual work, and perceptual ratings of agency, motivation, and utility. Short-term pre-to-post percentage changes were computed for each measure. VHF straight-line training produced the largest reductions in normalized path length (-4.69%) and completion time (-6.12%), whereas VHF sinusoid training produced the largest reductions in movement jerk (-5.67%) and virtual work (-13.33%). ASF modality affected path length, completion time, jerk, EMG amplitude, and virtual work, whereas task difficulty modulated beta-band EEG power and the physiological index. Changes in path length were positively associated with changes in completion time and EMG amplitude. These findings suggest that ASF modality and task difficulty can differentially shape short-term behavioral, physiological, and perceptual responses in healthy participants. The exploratory distribution of participant-specific best-case conditions motivates future studies using independent trial subsets to evaluate whether behavioral and physiological measures can support individualized VR training.

papers.title: Nutritional status, health literacy, and lifestyle factors associated with health-related quality of life in patients with decompensated cirrhosis: a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Liver cirrhosis is one of the leading causes of liver-related mortality worldwide. The disease typically progresses from an initially asymptomatic, compensated phase to decompensation, which adversely affects patients' health-related quality of life (HRQoL). Identifying the factors that influence HRQoL and implementing effective interventions are essential for improving patient outcomes. Based on the health ecology theory, this study focuses on health literacy and nutritional status, with the aim of enhancing patients' quality of survival through targeted interventions. A cross-sectional design was employed, using convenience sampling to recruit 202 patients with decompensated cirrhosis. Data collection included demographic information, biochemical indicators, and scores on health literacy, nutritional status, and HRQoL. Using IBM SPSS Statistics version 27, correlation analysis and multiple linear regression were conducted to primarily explore the associations of nutritional status, health literacy, and lifestyle factors with HRQoL. Correlation analysis showed that health literacy, nutritional status, sleep quality, and physical activity were significantly associated with patients' quality of life. Multiple linear regression revealed that nutritional status was independently associated with the HRQoL; notably, the model's explanatory power for HRQoL significantly increased (R Square increment) when health literacy was introduced, indicating practical significance. Furthermore, regression analyses showed that communication ability (B = -0.177, p = 0.007), walking (B = -1.589, p = 0.007), and aerobic exercise (B = -1.739, p = 0.017) as significant predictors of the physical dimension. Poor sleep significantly predicted both dimensions (physical: B = 1.193, p = 0.032; psychological: B = 0.532, p = 0.001), while information acquisition ability (B = -0.028, p = 0.021) specifically predicted the psychological dimension. This study demonstrated that both health literacy and nutritional status were significantly associated with the HRQoL among patients with decompensated cirrhosis. These findings may inform the design of targeted interventions to enhance health literacy and nutritional status, which may be beneficial for promoting self-management and improving clinical outcomes. Furthermore, they support the development of individualized management strategies.

papers.title: Birth of the Nigerian Sleep Society: A Milestone for Sleep Medicine in Nigeria and Africa.
papers.abstract: Sleep disorders are significant and are of major public health concern with high socioeconomic impact. However, they are under-recognised and under-treated in Nigeria and most of Africa, because of poor access to sleep specialists, sleep studies and limited treatment options. Prior to the inauguration of the Nigerian Sleep Society in 2025, there was no formal framework for sleep professionals in West Africa. Activities were on community engagement, awareness campaigns, meetings and scientific discussions on sleep health-related topical issues, training programs, collaborations, and publication of sleep health data, applicable to sub-Saharan Africa. Following the inauguration, the society is strategically positioned to address the critical barriers specifically affecting sleep medicine in West Africa, such as low community awareness, high costs of care, limited diagnostic capacity, insufficient training programs, inadequate sleep specialists, non-structured sleep health curriculum for undergraduates and postgraduates, lack of certification of sleep medicine personnel and inadequate research data. In this article, we explored the epidemiology of sleep disorder, the need for the Nigerian Sleep Society, its historical perspectives, and the strategic vision for addressing sleep disorders and the future pathway for sleep medicine in Nigeria and Africa.

papers.title: Comparative effects of exercise modalities on sleep quality in middle-aged and older adults with sleep disorders: A systematic review with pairwise, network, and dose-responsemeta-analyses.
papers.abstract: Exercise may improve sleep quality in middle-aged and older adults with sleep disorders, but the comparative effects of different exercise modalities and the dose-response relationship remain unclear. We systematically searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library from inception to May 2026. Eligible studies were randomized controlled trials examining the effects of exercise interventions on sleep quality in middle-aged and older adults with sleep disorders. Two independent reviewers assessed study quality, and random-effects pairwise, network, and dose-response meta-analyses were performed to evaluate the effects of different exercise interventions and doses on sleep quality. The analysis included 23 randomized controlled trials involving 1,478 middle-aged and older adults with sleep disorders. Pairwise meta-analysis showed that exercise reduced Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) and Insomnia Severity Index (ISI) scores but had no significant effect on Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS) scores. Bayesian network meta-analysis showed that, compared with the control group, aerobic exercise (SMD = 1.34, 95% CrI: 0.86∼1.82), mind-body exercise (SMD = 0.64, 95% CrI: 0.30∼0.97), and combined exercise (SMD = 0.60, 95% CrI: 0.13∼1.07) may improve PSQI scores. The dose-response analysis suggested an inverted U-shaped association, with the largest predicted effect occurring near 539 MET-min/week within the observed dose range. Low-to moderate-certainty evidence suggests that aerobic, mind-body, and combined exercise may reduce PSQI scores, with a nonlinear dose-response relationship.
papers.journal: Journal of exercise science and fitness

papers.title: Fetal and neonatal outcomes of pregnancies complicated by maternal sleep-disordered breathing: a systematic review.
papers.abstract: Maternal obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and the broader spectrum of sleep-disordered breathing (SDB) during pregnancy may be associated with fetal and neonatal outcomes, but the literature is heterogeneous and uses clinically distinct exposure definitions. This systematic review aimed to evaluate associations between maternal SDB and fetal/neonatal outcomes while preserving differences in exposure ascertainment. Following PRISMA 2020, the review was re-audited using updated PubMed and Web of Science searches, backward and forward citation searching, and ClinicalTrials.gov and WHO ICTRP registry searches. Exposures were classified as (1) objectively confirmed OSA/SDB, (2) administrative-code-defined OSA, and (3) symptom-, snoring-, or questionnaire-defined SDB risk. No meta-analysis was conducted because clinically comparable subsets were insufficient for quantitative pooling. The completed re-audit identified 64 eligible publications mapped to 53 conservative cohort/dataset families (55 if two probable overlap pairs are treated as separate): 22 objective/physiologic, 11 administrative/clinical, and 31 symptom/questionnaire publications. Objective studies showed mixed findings, with fetal-growth or neonatal signals in selected cohorts but null findings in several other objectively assessed populations. Administrative-code OSA was repeatedly associated with preterm birth and selected neonatal outcomes, although exposure misclassification and residual confounding remain important. Symptom/questionnaire studies were heterogeneous, with associations varying by symptom definition, timing, and outcome. Current evidence does not establish a consistent fetal or neonatal risk pattern for objectively confirmed maternal OSA/SDB. Administrative-code and symptom/questionnaire evidence suggests associations for selected outcomes, particularly preterm birth, but should not be interpreted as a single homogeneous OSA effect. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420251110706.

papers.title: Validation and modification of a Chinese smell identification test (CSIT-12) in patients with Parkinson's disease and rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder.
papers.abstract: To enhance olfactory screening for Chinese patients with Parkinson's disease (PD) or rapid-eye movement sleep behavior disorder (RBD) by developing and modifying a Chinese Smell Identification Test 12 (CSIT-12). In a discovery cohort, 69 PD patients and 47 healthy controls (HCs) were tested on 24 distinct odors using the Sniffin' Sticks Screening Test 12 (SSST-12) and CSIT-12. The 12 odors with the highest area under the curve (AUC) were selected to construct the Chinese version of the Sniffin' Sticks Screening Test 12 (C-SSST-12). This newly developed test was then validated in an independent cohort comprising 48 PD patients, 48 RBD patients, and 48 HCs. The reliability and validity of SSST-12, CSIT-12, C-SSST-12, and further abbreviated odor subsets were compared. Scores on SSST-12, CSIT-12, and C-SSST-12 were significantly lower in both PD and RBD compared to HCs (all P < 0.001). Both the CSIT-12 and SSST-12 demonstrated good discriminative capacity for PD versus HCs (CSIT-12: AUC = 0.832, sensitivity = 77.1%, specificity = 83.3%; SSST-12: AUC = 0.913, sensitivity = 85.4%, specificity = 81.3%) and RBD versus HCs (CSIT-12: AUC = 0.881, sensitivity = 85.4%, specificity = 83.3%; SSST-12: AUC = 0.893, sensitivity = 79.2%, specificity = 81.3%). Notably, the C-SSST-12 achieved the highest discriminative performance for PD versus HCs (AUC = 0.930, sensitivity = 81.3%, specificity = 85.4%) and RBD versus HCs (AUC = 0.949, sensitivity = 89.6%, specificity = 85.4%). A 5-odor CSIT-12 subset and a 3-odor C-SSST-12 subset retained high discriminative validity. This study highlights the discriminative value of utilizing culturally familiar odors for the screening of PD and RBD in Chinese populations. Furthermore, the abbreviated odor subsets offer highly efficient, rapid screening options suitable for community-based testing and fast-paced clinical environments.

papers.title: Aging in Autism: An Event-Related Potentials Study of Auditory Change Detection.
papers.abstract: Autistic individuals are often thought to exhibit reduced tolerance for change, which may stem from atypicalities in sensory processing, particularly in the detection of environmental changes. Within the predictive coding framework, this intolerance may reflect altered generation and updating internal predictions in response to sensory input, leading to increased prediction errors. Mismatch negativity and the P3a component are event-related potentials (ERPs) indexing automatic auditory change detection and involuntary attention shift. While studied in autistic children and young adults, little is known about how these components evolve during aging, an important gap as 21 million autistic adults over 60 are expected by 2050. This study examined mismatch negativity and P3a responses in 43 autistic adults (aged 21-64) and 60 nonautistic adults (aged 20-69) using a passive auditory oddball paradigm with standard (1000 Hz) and deviant (1100 Hz; p = 0.15) tones. Electroencephalography recording revealed no significant differences between autistic and nonautistic individuals on mismatch negativity and P3a amplitude or latency. However, mismatch negativity amplitude decreased with age over frontal site, similarly across both groups. No age-related effects were found for mismatch negativity latency or P3a measures in either group. These findings suggest that, from adulthood onward, the neural mechanisms underlying automatic change detection and preattentional processes are similar in both autistic and nonautistic adults, and that their overall time course of aging appears comparable, supporting the parallel aging hypothesis. Nonetheless, future research should explore how these preserved neural responses relate to behavioral reactivity to change in autism.

papers.title: Pre-sleep milk-derived proteins do not impair sleep or recovery in elite female athletes.
papers.abstract: Sleep is essential for athlete recovery and performance, yet athletes frequently experience restricted or poor-quality sleep. Pre-sleep feeding (PSF) has emerged as a strategy to support recovery, but randomized, double-blinded, crossover trials comparing PSF macronutrient options on objective and subjective sleep outcomes in elite female athletes remain limited. Twenty-five National Collegiate Athletic Association (NCAA) Division I female athletes (18-25 years old) were recruited; 21 completed the trial. In a randomized, double-blinded, placebo controlled, crossover design conducted over 4-8 weeks, participants consumed four treatments for three consecutive nights each: 40 g casein protein (CAS; 160 kcal), 40 g α-lactalbumin protein (ALA; 160 kcal), 40 g carbohydrate (CHO; 160 kcal), and 40g of a placebo (PLA; 5 kcal), with a minimum three-day washout between conditions. Supplements were consumed ~2 h after the final meal and ~30 min before bedtime as the last caloric intake of the day. Objective outcomes were obtained from the WHOOP 4.0 device (total sleep time (TST), sleep onset latency (SOL), sleep efficiency (SE), resting heart rate (RHR), and heart rate variability (HRV)). Subjective outcomes were assessed each morning via questionnaires (subjective sleep quality (SSQ), subjective sleep onset latency (SSOL), and subjective recovery (SREC)). Nocturnal interstitial glucose was assessed via blinded continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) in a subset (n = 6). Sleep and recovery variables were analyzed using one-way repeated-measures analysis of variance (ANOVA) to evaluate treatment effects across the four supplementation conditions. For CGM data, a two-way repeated-measures ANOVA was used to evaluate main effects of treatment and time, as well as the treatment × time interaction. Tukey's post hoc testing was used with significance set at p < 0.05. No significant treatment effects were observed for TST, SOL, SE, RHR, or HRV (p > 0.05). TST ranged from 7.47-7.62 h, SE from 91.5-92.0%, RHR from 53.5-54.1 bpm, and HRV from 98.2-103.9 ms across conditions. No significant treatment effects were detected for SSQ, SSOL, or SREC (p > 0.05); SSQ ranged from 69-75%, SSOL from 16-20 min, and SREC from 61-66%. In the CGM sub-analysis, a main effect of time was observed for nocturnal glucose (p = 0.008), but no differences among treatments (p = 0.187) or a time × treatment interaction (p = 0.550) were detected. In NCAA Division I female athletes, three consecutive nights of pre-sleep ingestion of CAS, ALA, or CHO did not impair objective or subjective measures of sleep or recovery compared with PLA. These findings demonstrate that pre-sleep feeding, regardless of macronutrient type, can be incorporated without negatively affecting sleep quality or recovery metrics. papers.title: The effect of text-picture consistency on memory integration in college students: Evidence from ERPs.
papers.abstract: In multimedia learning, individuals often need to integrate textual and visual information. The neural mechanisms underlying how consistency between text and pictures affects memory integration remain unclear. To examine the effect of text-picture consistency on memory integration in college students and to determine the processing time at which this effect occurs. Totally 28 Chinese college students (nfemale = 20, nmale = 8; Mage = 21.64 ± 2.30) participated in this experiment. An adapted pictorial demonstration paradigm was employed. Participants sequentially learned two pairs of text-picture stem facts (consistent vs. inconsistent), separated by an interval, followed by a recognition test for stem and integrated facts. Behavioural and event-related potential (ERP) data were recorded simultaneously. Under the text-picture consistency condition, college students showed significantly better memory integration performance than under the inconsistency condition (58% vs. 48%). EEG results showed that the text-picture inconsistency condition (i.e., the picture and text within a single stem fact were semantically mismatched) elicited a larger P600 wave (500-800 ms) than the text-picture consistency condition, suggesting that text-picture inconsistency primarily induces conflict and integration difficulties during late cognitive processing. No significant differences were observed in the early N400 component. Text-picture consistency facilitates memory integration primarily during late processing, aligning with cognitive theories of multimedia learning. Educationally, it serves as a key quality indicator for multimedia material design. Instructors should prioritize semantic alignment and assess knowledge integration during evaluation.
papers.journal: The British journal of educational psychology

papers.title: Clinical and Research Trends in Adult Acupressure Randomized Controlled Trials: A Scoping and Bibliometric Review.
papers.abstract: Acupressure has gained increasing attention as a noninvasive, low-risk, and cost-effective complementary intervention to address persistent symptoms such as pain, anxiety, fatigue, and sleep disturbances among adults. Although the volume of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating acupressure has grown substantially, an integrated synthesis that combines clinical evidence mapping with bibliometric characterization remains limited. This study aimed to conduct an integrated scoping review and bibliometric analysis of RCTs on acupressure interventions among adults in order to map the scope of clinical evidence and identify publication trends, thematic concentrations, and research collaboration patterns. This integrated scoping review was reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) Extension for Scoping Reviews reporting guideline. RCTs published between 2020 and 2025 were retrieved from the Scopus database using Population-Concept-Context (PCC) eligibility criteria. The included studies involved adults aged 18 years or older who received acupressure interventions in clinical or health care settings. Data extraction captured both clinical characteristics and bibliometric indicators. Descriptive synthesis was integrated with bibliometric analyses of annual publication trends, subject areas, geographic distribution, author productivity, collaboration networks, and keyword co-occurrence. A total of 303 RCTs were included. Publication output increased steadily, with a notable surge after 2022. Most studies were indexed within Medicine and Nursing. China, Iran, and the United States were the most productive countries, while international collaboration remained limited. Thematic analysis revealed that pain and musculoskeletal conditions were the dominant focuses, closely linked to quality-of-life outcomes. Psychological symptoms and sleep disturbances formed a strongly interconnected cluster, alongside emerging applications in women's health and chronic disease management. The evidence base for adult acupressure has expanded rapidly and demonstrates increasing thematic coherence. Future research should prioritize broader collaboration, diversified clinical applications, and implementation-oriented studies to enhance the translation of findings into practice.
papers.journal: Journal of integrative and complementary medicine

papers.title: Abstracts of the 28th Congress of the European Sleep Research Society, 20 - 23 October 2026, Maastricht, The Netherlands.
Beyond canonical homeostasis: Dynamic, plastic, and intermittently unregulated physiology as the norm.
papers.abstract: Homeostasis is often taught as steady-state regulation keeping internal variables within narrow limits-reflecting a mammalian bias. Yet, canonical homeostasis is far from universal. In many animals, including humans, normal physiological states allow some variables to fluctuate cyclically or stochastically while others remain tightly controlled. Indeed, across non-mammalian species, broad physiological variability is frequently normal rather than exceptional. Here we present case studies showing that plastic, variable regulation-sometimes approaching randomness-is both common and adaptive. Examples include intermittent breathing during diving, episodic feeding and digestion, pulsatile hormone release, variable sleep cycles, irregular gastric emptying, fluctuating renal blood flow, and stochastic immune responses. These complex regulatory patterns represent evolved strategies-not failures of homeostasis-allowing organisms to function efficiently in dynamic environments. Such flexible regulation, including unregulated intervals, may minimize energetic costs compared with continuous tight control, enhancing evolutionary fitness. We propose that variable degrees of physiological regulation have evolved as energy-efficient solutions shaped by natural selection. Expanding the concept of homeostasis to include intermittent and stochastic forms will improve our understanding of physiological adaptation, with significant implications for ecology and evolutionary biology. We further advocate new experimental approaches to distinguish adaptive variability from true regulatory failure.

papers.title: Burnout and second victim phenomenon in obstetrics: Psychological impact of maternal and perinatal adverse events, medico-legal stress, workplace violence, and organizational culture.
papers.abstract: Obstetrics is among the most psychologically demanding fields in medicine. Clinicians must safeguard the lives of both mother and fetus while managing unpredictable emergencies, life-threatening complications, and considerable medico-legal scrutiny. Repeated exposure to maternal and perinatal adverse events leaves obstetricians particularly vulnerable to burnout and the second victim phenomenon. This review examines the occupational stressors driving burnout in obstetrics, with particular attention to the second victim phenomenon, moral injury, medico-legal pressure, workplace violence, and the organizational factors that shape clinician well-being. A narrative review of English-language literature in PubMed and PubMed Central was conducted for studies published up to June 2026, using pre-specified search terms combined with reference-list screening of key publications; formal risk-of-bias assessment and protocol registration were not undertaken, consistent with a narrative rather than systematic review design. Burnout affects an estimated 40%-75% of obstetricians and gynecologists, and nearly 45% will experience the second victim phenomenon during their career, with 19% reporting an episode in the past year. Adverse obstetric events commonly provoke guilt, anxiety, sleep disturbance, and post-traumatic stress symptoms, compounded by long hours, litigation, workplace violence, moral injury, and dual responsibility for mother and fetus. These pressures drive defensive practice, reduced job satisfaction, medical errors, and workforce attrition. Structured peer-support programs, debriefing, Just Culture principles, and organizational wellness initiatives show promising, although largely observational, evidence of benefit. Burnout and second victim experiences are significant occupational hazards in obstetrics. Evidence-based organizational support is essential for clinician well-being, workforce retention, and the safety and quality of maternity care, although higher-quality, obstetric-specific intervention research is needed.

papers.title: Neurofeedback for Management of Musculoskeletal Pain: A Randomized Control Trial Using DOMS.
papers.abstract: Chronic musculoskeletal (MSK) pain is associated with maladaptive neuroplasticity, often reflected in altered alpha activity (8-13 Hz). Neurofeedback may offer a way to modulate this activity, yet most protocols target alpha activity during rest, despite movement being a common pain trigger. This study investigated whether neurofeedback during movement could modulate alpha activity and reduce pain in healthy individuals experiencing induced pain via delayed onset muscle soreness (DOMS). This experiment was a randomized, two-armed, parallel-group trial. Twenty-nine participants were included (15 females, mean age = 28 years). Exclusions included neurological, psychiatric, MSK conditions. Participants were randomly assigned to an intervention group (aiming to reduce alpha activity) or a control group (aiming to increase it). Alpha activity was assessed as the alpha power during rest and movement. DOMS was induced using eccentric exercise of muscle extensor carpi radialis in Session 1. Neurofeedback was administered in Session 2, where participants underwent three blocks of neurofeedback training, using individualized EEG-based visual feedback to modulate alpha activity. Session 3 assessed potential lasting neurofeedback effects. Pain was rated across the three sessions, which took place 24-48 h apart. DOMS induction was confirmed by increased pain (p < 0.001, r = 0.82) and reduced alpha activity during movement (p = 0.017, r = 0.49). Neurofeedback did not significantly alter alpha activity (p = 0.114, W = 0.05 for the control group, p = 0.338, W = 0.037 for the intervention group). A single neurofeedback session was insufficient to modulate brain activity or pain perception. Methodological factors, including limited training duration and participants' strategies, may have contributed to the lack of an observable effect. Although neurofeedback did not result in significant changes after one session, the observed alpha modulation following DOMS highlights the relevance of targeting neuroplasticity during MSK pain. Future studies should optimize training protocols and consider multisession designs to enhance clinical applicability.

papers.title: Clinical and Longitudinal Heterogeneity Within the Acute Outer Retinopathy Spectrum: A Three-Case Series.
papers.abstract: To describe three distinct presentations within the acute outer retinopathy (AOR) spectrum, emphasizing differences in stage, longitudinal evolution, and structure-function relationships. Retrospective case series. The first, a 14-year-old asymptomatic male, had bilateral sectoral and spot-like outer retinal lesions in the subacute-chronic stage. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) demonstrated outer nuclear layer thinning with ellipsoid and interdigitation zone disruption and focal retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) attenuation, without the angular sign of Henle fiber layer hyperreflectivity (ASHH). Fundus autofluorescence (FAF) revealed lesions with a hypoautofluorescent core and hyperautofluorescent border, while fluorescein angiography (FA) showed window-defect hyperfluorescence and focal venular wall staining. The second, a 20-year-old male, developed severe visual field loss after a viral illness. FAF showed perivenular outer retinal involvement, and OCT revealed perivenular disruption with ASHH documented at 11 months. Visual field deficits were severe and partially correlated with structural abnormalities, with incomplete recovery over 3 years. Pattern electroretinography showed borderline reduction, whereas full-field electroretinography was within the lower limits of normal. The third, a 43-year-old female, presented with acute visual symptoms and mild intraocular inflammation. FAF showed sectoral peripapillary hyperautofluorescence, with corresponding outer retinal disruption on OCT. FA demonstrated venular wall staining and optic disc hyperfluorescence without diffuse vascular leakage. Perimetry showed bilateral diffuse sensitivity loss, while electrophysiology demonstrated generalized cone-predominant photoreceptor dysfunction. These cases illustrate clinical and longitudinal heterogeneity within established AOR patterns, including asymptomatic subacute-chronic disease, perivenular disease with structure-function dissociation and late documentation of ASHH, and symptomatic sectoral disease with diffuse photoreceptor dysfunction.

papers.title: Early neurocognitive outcomes following SEEG with radiofrequency thermocoagulation.
papers.abstract: Characterization of early neuropsychological outcomes following SEEG with radiofrequency thermocoagulation (RFTHC) is essential to guide patient expectations around return to work, study, and caregiving. The current study aimed to describe the early neurocognitive sequelae of SEEG. Consecutive patients undergoing SEEG were prospectively recruited from two tertiary epilepsy centers in Melbourne, Australia. Patients were administered the Repeatable Battery for the Assessment of Neuropsychological Status (RBANS) via telehealth before and 3 weeks after SEEG (M = 19.69 days, SD = 4.41). Given the telehealth platform, the coding subtest was substituted for the Symbol Digit Modalities Test, and a modified score of global cognitive function was calculated. To evaluate group changes, paired sample t-tests were performed. Reliable change indices were computed to explore individual-level changes. Pearson's correlation coefficients evaluated relationships between change in global cognitive function and SEEG admission variables. SEEG patients were invited to complete a semi-structured interview canvassing the recovery following SEEG. Twenty-eight patients completed the neuropsychological examination (M = 37.89 years, SD = 9.72, range = 17-56 years, 54% female). All patients underwent RFTHC with a mean of 11.43 (SD = 6.87, range = 2-28) coagulation sites. At a whole group level, 3-weeks post SEEG there was no evidence for global nor domain-specific cognitive change. Reliable change indices with 90% confidence revealed only 4% (1/28) declined on at least two measures and 10% (3/28) showed psychometric improvement. Pearson's correlational coefficients showed no evidence for association between change in global cognitive function with SEEG factors including admission length, number of spontaneous or stimulated seizures, number of electrodes, or number of RFTHC sites. Subjective reports of language change tended to be accompanied by a decline on the RBANS language index that did not meet reliable change criteria. Most patients reported returning to work around 4 weeks post SEEG. By 3 weeks, gross cognitive functioning tends to be in keeping with pre-SEEG performances for most patients. These findings have direct clinical implications for SEEG neuropsychological counseling. SEEG is increasingly used to guide epilepsy surgery. Despite this, little is known about the cognitive recovery in the weeks following the procedure. We found that for most patients, broad cognitive functioning 3 weeks after SEEG with coagulation was consistent with function before SEEG, with only a small minority showing significant changes. Some people who reported language difficulties also showed a decline on language testing, although this was often small. Of those patients working before SEEG, most returned to work by 4 weeks. These results provide important evidence to guide patient counseling, recovery planning, and management after SEEG.

papers.title: Validation of the diagnosis of Lennox-Gastaut syndrome: Challenges and lessons learned.
papers.abstract: Lennox-Gastaut Syndrome (LGS) is a severe developmental and epileptic encephalopathy characterized by multiple seizure types, cognitive impairment, and distinct electroencephalographic (EEG) findings. However, evolving diagnostic criteria, heterogeneous clinical features, and inconsistent electronic health record (EHR) documentation complicate accurate diagnosis and cohort identification. As part of a Patient-Centered Outcomes Research Institute-sponsored study developing EHR-based computable phenotypes for LGS, we established a reference standard through retrospective chart review and epileptologist classification. A multicenter retrospective chart review was conducted across seven pediatric epilepsy centers. Stratified sampling using PCORnet data selected patients based on the International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision diagnosis code for LGS or other intractable epilepsy diagnoses between 2016 and 2022. Clinical teams abstracted seizure history, EEG findings, developmental status, and treatment history. Two epileptologists independently reviewed each case as classic LGS, pragmatic LGS, or not LGS. Discordant cases underwent adjudication by a senior epileptologist. Cases with incomplete or unclear data underwent repeat abstraction and review. Of 997 identified patients, 935 underwent classification after exclusions. Initial epileptologist disagreement occurred in 105 cases (11%, unweighted Cohen kappa = 82%). Following adjudication, 130 cases underwent reabstraction to retrieve additional EEG reports and clinical details. Rereview reclassified 67 cases initially considered "not LGS": 33 classic LGS, 12 pragmatic LGS, and 22 excluded for insufficient data. Key EHR challenges included inconsistent EEG reporting, incomplete seizure type characterization, fragmented documentation of cognitive impairment, unclear age at onset, and variable terminology across institutions and providers. Slow spike-and-wave EEG findings were the most frequently missing diagnostic element. Validating LGS diagnoses using EHR data is complex and resource intensive. Standardized terminology, structured documentation, and rigorous multicenter validation may improve diagnostic accuracy, research cohort identification, computable phenotype development, and longitudinal care for individuals with LGS. Our results highlight important operational lessons for multicenter rare epilepsy studies and underscore the need for improved diagnosis pathways and longitudinal care systems for those with LGS and their families.

papers.title: Analysis of Factors Influencing the Psychological State of Patients After Autologous Liver Transplantation.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND The use of ex vivo liver resection and autologous liver transplantation (ELRA) for end-stage hepatic alveolar echinococcosis is gradually increasing, while postoperative psychological disorders in these patients remain underrecognized. We prespecified that longer pre-transplant waiting time, postoperative complications, and higher transfusion volume would be associated with worse anxiety, depression, and sleep disturbance at 1 month after ELRA. MATERIAL AND METHODS This single-center retrospective study enrolled 138 patients who underwent ELRA from 2020 to 2025. We collected demographic data, perioperative clinical indexes, and scores at baseline and 1 month postoperatively using the Self-Rating Anxiety Scale (SAS), Self-Rating Depression Scale (SDS), Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HAMA), Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD), and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Univariate analysis and multivariate linear regression were used to identify independent influencing factors. RESULTS Longer pre-transplant waiting time independently predicted worse scores across all psychological and sleep scales (all P<0.05). Prolonged anhepatic phase duration was specifically associated with higher PSQI scores (P<0.05). Intraoperative transfusion showed marginal but nonsignificant associations, and postoperative complications were significant only in univariate analysis. CONCLUSIONS Longer pre‑transplant waiting time is the core and most consistent risk factor for poor mental health after ELRA, while prolonged anhepatic phase is specifically linked to postoperative sleep disturbance. These findings support the implementation of targeted, stage-specific psychological interventions, especially during the pre-transplant waiting period, to improve mental health and quality of life in patients undergoing ELRA.

papers.title: Is Less More? Exploring the Visual Processes of Minimalist and Complex Photography Through Eye Tracking and EEG.
papers.abstract: In a world filled with an overwhelming amount of visual information, the clean and distinctive visual style of minimalist photography stands out. However, empirical research on how minimalist style affects visual cognition and psychological responses remains limited. The present study investigated the effects of photographic style (minimalist versus complex) on viewers' visual behavior, emotional responses, and brainwave state by conducting quantitative psychological experiments. Thirty participants viewed photographs in one of the two styles. Eye-tracking, consumer-grade electroencephalography (EEG), and subjective psychological assessment data were collected, enabling comprehensive evaluation of how the participants looked at, responded to, and emotionally engaged with the images. At the level of visual behavior, minimalism elicited significantly reduced number of fixations and saccades, but the duration of a single fixation is significantly longer, and the heatmap hotspots are highly concentrated, presenting a focused processing pattern of fewer but longer gazes. On a psychological level, minimalism evoked significantly less feeling of complexity and greater relaxation, although there was no significant difference in the aesthetics score between the two styles. In terms of brainwave state, viewing minimalist images resulted in significantly higher attention eSense levels, while the meditation eSense level did not show a significant difference. The results of this study therefore show that minimalist composition may influence the visual search pattern to be more focused, which is compatible with the tendency of simplified organization predicted by the principle of simplification. This study not only deepens the theoretical understanding of the psychological mechanisms of minimalist aesthetics, but also provides practical reference for visual communication and image creation of minimalist composition serving as an effective strategy for guiding the eyes toward the core subject.

papers.title: The translational asymmetry of corpus callosotomy: Two literatures that answered different questions.
papers.abstract: Corpus callosotomy is an established palliative operation for drug-resistant epilepsy dominated by drop attacks, and it is performed in three extents: anterior, usually of the anterior two-thirds; total, in one or two stages; and selective posterior, which preserves the genu and rostral body. Meta-analysis finds no difference between them in overall seizure reduction, a difference in drop attack control favoring the posterior approach, and a graded difference in disconnection syndrome, but there has never been a prospective head-to-head comparison, and the optimal extent of section remains undefined. A search of PubMed, Embase, and the Web of Science Core Collection identified 62 experimental studies in which the corpus callosum or another forebrain commissure was sectioned with an epilepsy-related outcome, spanning 1948-2026 across six species and every major seizure model. This literature is neither absent nor recent. What it has almost never done is vary the extent of section: the few studies that varied it took the laterality of kindling transfer or of interictal synchrony as the endpoint, never seizure control and never cognitive cost. No study compares the three extents against a common outcome; none models the selective posterior operation as it is defined clinically; none randomizes between extents; and none combines graded disconnection with time-locked bilateral electrophysiology, diffusion-based verification of the fibers divided, and a behavioral read-out in the same animals. The effect of section is also bidirectional: focal seizures may intensify through loss of transcallosal inhibition, and in the pentylenetetrazol model callosal section paradoxically facilitates convulsions, which limits chemoconvulsant preparations. The asymmetry between the clinical and experimental literatures is therefore one of method rather than of volume or attention: the two answered different questions, and the question the clinical field now asks requires a manipulation the experimental literature has never performed. PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY: Surgeons can treat severe epilepsies by cutting the bundle of fibers that joins the two halves of the brain, but they do not agree on how much of it to cut. We searched three databases and found 62 animal studies of this operation going back to 1948. Almost none of them compared different amounts of cutting, and none looked at the newest version of the operation. Answering the surgeons' question will require a new kind of animal experiment rather than more reading of the old ones.

papers.title: Design, Synthesis, and Biological Evaluation of Quinolin-2-One-Indole Schiff Base Hybrids as Potential EGFR-Targeted Anticancer Agents Against Breast and Ovarian Cancer.
papers.abstract: A series of new quinolin-2-one-indole Schiff base hybrids was designed, synthesized, and tested as potential anticancer agents targeting the epidermal growth factor receptor. The designed compounds were synthesized via a multistep synthetic route comprising phenylhydrazone formation, Fischer indole cyclization, Vilsmeier-Haack formylation, and subsequent Schiff base condensation. Structural elucidation was performed using IR, 1H NMR, 13C NMR, and mass spectral analysis. In silico studies demonstrated that the synthesized compounds exhibited strong binding affinities to both wild-type (PDB ID: 1M17) and mutant EGFR (PDB ID: 4ZAU), as evidenced by favorable docking scores, with PYd2 showing the strongest interaction. Molecular dynamics simulations over 100 ns further confirmed that the PYd2-EGFR complexes remained stable, maintaining consistent protein-ligand contacts and exhibiting stable RMSD and RMSF values throughout the simulation period. Predicted ADME-toxicity profiles demonstrated favorable drug-like properties, oral absorption, and acceptable toxicity profiles for most synthesized derivatives. In vitro anticancer evaluation against MDA-MB-231 and SK-OV-3 cell lines identified PYd2 as the most potent analog. ELISA-based studies demonstrated significant inhibition of EGFR expression and phosphorylation, while DAPI staining revealed characteristic apoptotic nuclear changes in treated cells. Overall, PYd2 showed favorable predicted EGFR binding and antiproliferative activity against both cancer cell lines.

papers.title: Tirzepatide for Obstructive Sleep Apnea: Trial Evidence, Cardiometabolic Effects, and Implications for Cardiovascular Practice.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea affects approximately one billion adults worldwide and is associated with hypertension, atrial fibrillation, heart failure, and stroke. Obesity is its dominant reversible cause, yet positive airway pressure therapy splints the pharyngeal airway without addressing the adiposity that narrows it, and randomized trials have not shown that it reduces cardiovascular events. In December 2024, the United States Food and Drug Administration approved tirzepatide, a dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, as the first drug for moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea in adults with obesity. We summarize the pharmacology of tirzepatide and the anatomic basis by which weight reduction improves upper airway patency, notably reduction of tongue and parapharyngeal fat. We then review the SURMOUNT-OSA program: two parallel 52-week, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trials enrolling 469 adults with obesity and an apnea-hypopnea index of at least 15 events per hour, one conducted without positive airway pressure and one during established positive airway pressure use. Tirzepatide reduced the apnea-hypopnea index by an estimated 20.0 and 23.8 events per hour relative to placebo, with concurrent reductions in sleep apnea-specific hypoxic burden, body weight, systolic blood pressure, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein.

papers.title: Mapping mental health complexity in esports: an exploratory psychosocial network approach.
papers.abstract: The rapid rise in popularity of esports has brought increased attention to the unique mental health challenges faced by esports players, yet research in this area remains in its infancy. Early research suggests a substantial mental health burden and has examined associations between esports-specific stressors, mental health, and sleep disturbances. However, much of this work has relied on traditional methodologies, providing limited insight into how affective, psychosocial, sleep-related, and esports-specific indicators are organised within this competitive performance environment. To address this gap, we developed a bespoke 17-item questionnaire tailored for Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) network analysis, an exploratory approach for mapping the conditional dependency structure of complex multivariate systems such as mental health. A total of 1025 esports players from over 60 countries completed the survey. Game-related thought preoccupation, a core feature of gaming disorder, emerged as the most robust structural sink node, downstream of several psychosocial indicators, raising the hypothesis that it represents a compound indicator of broader upstream psychosocial strain. Depressed mood occupied an upstream position within the network, an observation that held more robustly for the psychopathological subnetwork as a whole than for depressed mood as the single source. Mental fatigue occupied an intermediate, connecting position between affective variables and the sleep and fatigue indicators. Its high prevalence, together with a positioning upstream of the sleep indicators, suggests that it may warrant closer examination in future research on training load, recovery, and sleep in esports, though this ordering rested on edges with moderate directional support. Emotion control and a sense of autonomy appeared to connect upstream affective distress with downstream esports-specific indicators such as esports-related stress, though was the least stable of the structural features identified. Collectively, these findings provide an exploratory map of how mental health-relevant indicators were organised in this performance environment, and generate concrete, testable hypotheses for future longitudinal, experimental, and intervention research.
keywords: Bayesian network; Depression; Directed Acyclic Graph; Emotion regulation; Esports; Game preoccupation; Mental fatigue; Mental health; Psychosocial network analysis; Sleep

papers.title: Childhood-onset parkinsonism, dystonia and severe muscle wasting in a Sudanese girl caused by a novel homozygous DnaJ heat shock protein family (heat shock protein 40) member C6 frameshift variant, with an incidental pathogenic breast cancer 1 gene secondary finding: a case report.
papers.abstract: DNAJC6-related juvenile parkinsonism is a rare autosomal recessive disorder of auxilin, a co-chaperone essential for clathrin-mediated synaptic vesicle recycling. Fewer than 50 kindreds have been reported worldwide, and the condition is easily missed when first-line investigations come back normal. We describe a Sudanese adolescent in whom a previously unreported homozygous DNAJC6 frameshift variant was identified only after a prolonged diagnostic journey that included a period during which her illness was mistakenly attributed to a functional neurological disorder. Clinical whole-exome sequencing additionally returned an incidental medically actionable BRCA1 secondary finding. A 13-year-old Sudanese girl, the eldest child of first-cousin parents, was born preterm and ventilated neonatally for severe respiratory distress. Her development was normal until age five, when an isolated upper-limb tremor first appeared. Over the next 8 years her condition progressed into severe juvenile parkinsonism: bilateral rest-and-action tremor, rigidity, bradykinesia, generalized dystonia with prominent oromandibular involvement, dysphagia, profound cachexia, cognitive and behavioral decline, sleep and autonomic disturbance, episodic oculogyric crises and three discrete seizures. By approximately 11 she was wheelchair-dependent. Earlier, unrevealing investigations had led to a psychiatric diagnosis of functional neurological disorder, and the dopamine antagonists prescribed on that basis worsened her condition. Whole-exome sequencing later identified a novel homozygous DNAJC6 frameshift deletion (NM_001256864.2:c.1480del; p.Glu494ArgfsTer12), absent from population databases, alongside a heterozygous pathogenic BRCA1 deletion reported as an actionable secondary finding. Levodopa produced partial motor benefit, complicated by on-state dyskinesias, visual hallucinations and excessive daytime somnolence. Subsequent up-titration of carbidopa/levodopa to approximately 5-hourly dosing produced a further, clinically evident improvement in gait and fine-motor function. This case adds a previously unreported allele to the DNAJC6 catalog and characterizes the severe end of its phenotype, where corticospinal signs and life-threatening cachexia accompany the more familiar extrapyramidal features. It illustrates the harm that follows premature labeling of a progressive organic movement disorder as functional, especially when dopamine antagonists are then prescribed. The accompanying pathogenic BRCA1 secondary finding shows the dual diagnostic yield that clinical whole-exome sequencing can deliver. Early genetic investigation in childhood-onset movement disorders, particularly with consanguinity, should be the rule, and cascade pathways for actionable secondary findings embedded in routine practice.

papers.title: Circadian clock and its potential as a therapy for ischemic heart disease.
papers.abstract: According to an epidemiological survey, myocardial infarction, ischemia-reperfusion injury, and aortic rupture usually occur in the morning and summer and are characterized by more severe symptoms and poorer prognosis. The occurrence, development, treatment difficulties, and poor prognosis of ischemic heart disease are closely related to circadian rhythm disorders and the abnormal transcription of circadian clock genes. Normal circadian rhythms regulate neurohumoral regulation and energy metabolism, thereby playing a protective or modulatory role in ischemic heart disease (IHD). HIF1α links the IHD and circadian signaling pathways through the hypoxia response element (HRE) and Per-Arnt-Sim (PAS) domains in gene promoters and enhancers.

papers.title: Frailty transitions and the risk of multisystem burden of chronic disease: a prospective cohort study in China.
papers.abstract: Frailty, defined by a decline in physiological reserve, is a key determinant of adverse health outcomes in older populations. While baseline frailty has been shown to predict the development of chronic diseases, the impact of changes in frailty status over time, particularly in rapidly ageing populations like China, remains poorly understood. This study aimed to assess how baseline frailty and its longitudinal transitions influence the incidence of chronic diseases across multiple organ systems. We analysed data from 17,708 adults (aged ≥ 40) in the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) collected between 2011 and 2018. Frailty was assessed using the Rockwood Frailty Index at baseline and at two-year follow-up, categorised as stable, improved, or worsened. We applied Cox proportional hazards models to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for the onset of 13 major chronic diseases spanning cardiovascular, metabolic, respiratory, neurological, psychiatric, digestive, renal, and musculoskeletal systems. The study included 9,807 to 16,882 participants across 13 disease-specific subgroups, with a median follow-up period of 6.2-6.8 years for baseline frailty status and 4.4-5.0 years for frailty transitions. Frail individuals were typically older, more likely to be female, unmarried, with lower education, higher BMI, and reported fewer hours of sleep. Baseline frailty was associated with significantly higher risks for all 13 chronic diseases, with the strongest association observed for psychiatric problems (HR 5.17, 95% CI 3.24-8.24). Worsening frailty over time was linked to elevated risks, particularly for asthma (HR 3.91, 95% CI 1.28-11.91), while improvements in frailty showed reduced risks, notably for kidney diseases (HR 0.37, 95% CI 0.22-0.63). The association was particularly strong in adults aged 40-65 years, indicating greater potential for risk modification in midlife. Frailty is a dynamic and modifiable predictor of multisystem chronic disease risk. Changes in frailty status offer valuable insights into future disease development, especially among middle-aged adults. Routine frailty monitoring in clinical settings may offer a strategic opportunity to delay or prevent the onset of chronic diseases through timely interventions. These findings emphasize the need for incorporating frailty-targeted strategies into public health and clinical care policies to enhance ageing-related disease prevention.
